title: SCIENTIFIC AND METHODOLOGICAL APPROACHES IN REFORMING THE UKRAINIAN SYSTEM OF PUBLIC PROCUREMENT IN THE PROCESS OF JOINING THE EU
summary: The transformation of procurement from technical tools to strategic mechanisms for economic stability and national defense requires modernizing evaluation systems. To secure financial resilience during EU integration, states must reform con
content: The transformation of procurement from technical tools to strategic mechanisms for economic stability and national defense requires modernizing evaluation systems. To secure financial resilience during EU integration, states must reform control frameworks. The article aims to substantiate scientific and methodological approaches to reforming the Ukrainian system of public procurement in the process of joining the EU. The methodology employs institutional analysis of legislation, ensemble machine learning, and quantitative operational audit evaluation. Developing these scientific and methodological approaches for Ukraine allows for shifting to real-time automated monitoring and reducing systemic corruption. Implementing the proposed risk-oriented tools in defense and civil sectors optimizes budget expenditures, supports national supply chain sovereignty, and facilitates post-war recovery.

title: Health and Quality of Life in Contemporary Society: Health Promotion, Lifestyles, and the Role of the Brazilian Unified Health System
summary: Health and quality of life in contemporary society are influenced by complex interactions between biological characteristics, individual behaviours, social relationships, economic conditions, environmental factors, and public policies. Chan
content: Health and quality of life in contemporary society are influenced by complex interactions between biological characteristics, individual behaviours, social relationships, economic conditions, environmental factors, and public policies. Changes in work patterns, urbanization, technological development, food environments, sedentary behaviour, population ageing, and increasing mental health demands have transformed the determinants of health and created new challenges for public health systems. In Brazil, the Unified Health System plays a fundamental role in promoting health, preventing diseases, reducing inequalities, and ensuring access to comprehensive care. This academic essay discusses health and quality of life from a contemporary public health perspective, emphasizing health promotion, lifestyles, social determinants, mental health, physical activity, nutrition, sleep, digital technologies, environmental conditions, and the role of SUS. Health promotion is understood as a collective responsibility that extends beyond individual behavioural choices and requires supportive social, economic, and environmental conditions. The discussion highlights the importance of Primary Health Care, intersectoral action, community participation, equity, and health education. Strengthening health promotion within SUS is essential for improving population well-being and addressing the increasingly complex determinants of health in contemporary societies.

title: Tax Refunds, Long‐Term Bank Loans and Firm R&D Intensity: Evidence From Chinese High‐Tech Listed Firms
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines whether realized tax refunds are associated with higher R&D intensity among Chinese high‐tech listed firms, and whether long‐term bank borrowing weakens part of this relationship. Using panel data for 957 A‐shar
content: ABSTRACT This study examines whether realized tax refunds are associated with higher R&D intensity among Chinese high‐tech listed firms, and whether long‐term bank borrowing weakens part of this relationship. Using panel data for 957 A‐share high‐tech firms from 2011 to 2023, we find that tax refunds scaled by total assets are positively associated with firm R&D intensity. The estimates also show that tax refunds are positively associated with long‐term bank loans, while long‐term bank loans are negatively associated with R&D intensity after controlling for firm characteristics, year effects and industry effects. We therefore interpret long‐term borrowing as a potential offsetting channel rather than as definitive causal mediation. Additional mechanism tests suggest that this offset is related to financing structure and financing constraints, and heterogeneity tests show stronger debt‐related crowding‐out patterns among state‐owned, smaller and younger firms. The findings highlight both the innovation‐supporting role of fiscal relief and the importance of credit‐market frictions in shaping its effectiveness.

title: Determinant of artificial intelligence skills adoption among built environment professionals in a developing economy
source: Journal of Information Technology Case and Application Research
summary: The demand for artificial intelligence (AI) competencies is increasing alongside the growing emphasis on sustainability, efficiency, and resilience in construction project delivery. Despite expanding research on digital transformation in co
content: The demand for artificial intelligence (AI) competencies is increasing alongside the growing emphasis on sustainability, efficiency, and resilience in construction project delivery. Despite expanding research on digital transformation in construction, limited empirical studies have examined the factors influencing AI skills adoption among built environment professionals, particularly in developing economies. This study investigates the determinants of AI skills adoption among built environment professionals in Nigeria. A quantitative research design was employed, with data collected through structured questionnaires administered to construction professionals. Descriptive and inferential statistical techniques were used for data analysis. Exploratory factor analysis revealed four key determinants of AI skills adoption: AI skills awareness and readiness, attitudinal readiness, institutional and policy environment, and resource accessibility factors. The findings provide valuable insights for policymakers, professional bodies, and higher education institutions seeking to enhance digital competencies and accelerate AI adoption within the construction sector, thereby supporting improved productivity, sustainability, and innovation.

title: Culture-free single-cell transcriptomics shows short term functional and associative stability in non-model microeukaryotes under shading stress
summary: Microeukaryotes are abundant, diverse, and morphologically and functionally complex. They represent one of the largest groups of primary producers and are involved in major ecosystem functions such as nutrient transformations and maintenanc
content: Microeukaryotes are abundant, diverse, and morphologically and functionally complex. They represent one of the largest groups of primary producers and are involved in major ecosystem functions such as nutrient transformations and maintenance of food webs. Although ~74,000 species of microeukaryotes are estimated to exist, very few are available in culture and only ~3000 are represented by reference genomes and transcriptomes. This limited representation significantly hinders the study of microeukaryotes in their natural environments. Single-cell transcriptomics with sequencing of full-length transcripts has potential to bypass this limitation. In this study, we employ Smart-seq3xpress for taxonomic identification and functional characterization of non-model mixotrophic freshwater microeukaryotes in a culture-free and reference-free manner, while also enabling inferences to be made for their prokaryotic associations. Computational analyses revealed 22 distinct microeukaryote taxa upon sequencing of 1520 randomly sampled cells, with assemblies of 12 good quality de novo partial transcriptomes, followed by functional annotation using sequence and structure homology. Gene expression analysis of the transcriptome for the most abundant microeukaryote in the sample, Rhodomonas, revealed a transcriptomic dip a few hours after experimental shading, followed by a gradual recovery in the next few days. Compared to samples in illuminated conditions, there was widespread downregulation of photosynthesis-, lysosome-, and carbon metabolism-related pathways in the shade, but the prevailing associations with prokaryotic lineages was unaffected by the light conditions. The different microeukaryotes, all present in the same environmental sample, featured distinct prokaryotic associates that were consistent across illumination conditions. This reference-free and culture-free study of 22 different microeukaryotic taxa sets the stage for high-throughput single cell transcriptomics to study microeukaryotic diversity in complex natural ecosystems, for their population-level taxonomic identity, sub-population-level transcriptomic profiles and metabolic states, and individual-level prokaryotic associations.

title: Corporate Debt Financing and Capital Structure Optimization for Large-Scale Infrastructure Investment under Saudi Vision 2030
summary: The financing arrangements required by the major infrastructure projects described in Saudi Vision 2030 must be such as to draw in a large amount of private capital without ending up with leverage positions that weaken should there be chang
content: The financing arrangements required by the major infrastructure projects described in Saudi Vision 2030 must be such as to draw in a large amount of private capital without ending up with leverage positions that weaken should there be changes in interest rates, construction costs, demand, or the circumstances under which the debt can be refinanced. This study examines how corporate debt financing and the structure of capital can be improved for the Saudi infrastructure sponsors and the project companies in question. In order to bring together the findings relating to leverage, debt maturity, project finance, sukuk and bonds, risk allocation, refinancing, and sustainability-linked finance, a systematic and integrated review of studies and evidence from Saudi institutions published between 2020 and 2025 was conducted. The evidence indicates that there is no single debt ratio which is optimal in all situations. The level of debt that can be taken on in infrastructure projects varies according to the stability and the quality of the contractual terms of the project's cash flows, the degree of construction and operating risk, the strength of the sponsor, the availability of collateral, the matching of maturities, currency exposure, and the credibility of the risk-sharing arrangements. Even though Saudi Arabia's rapidly expanding sukuk and debt markets increase the range of financing alternatives available, the growing volume of issuances also makes it more necessary to maintain disciplined debt service coverage, keep sufficient liquidity buffers, and plan for refinancing. The review proposes a dynamic optimisation framework which treats the capital structure as a decision that should be made throughout the whole lifecycle of the project rather than as a single, one-off decision regarding funding. It recommends combining specific leverage limits for each project, long-term debt, a variety of funding sources, clear risk allocation, and periodic re-optimisation. This approach will help to lower funding costs on a risk-adjusted basis while at the same time protecting the company's solidity and encouraging private sector participation in the infrastructure projects under Vision 2030.

title: Analysis on the Influence Mechanism of Supply Chain Finance on Enterprises’ Green Technology Innovation
source: International Journal of World Economic Research
summary: Green technological innovation serves as the driving force for enterprises’ green transformation and high quality development, and supply chain financing provides guarantees for green technological innovation. Taking Chinese A share listed
content: Green technological innovation serves as the driving force for enterprises’ green transformation and high quality development, and supply chain financing provides guarantees for green technological innovation. Taking Chinese A share listed firms on the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges from 2012 to 2024 as research samples, this paper empirically analyzes the impact effect and mechanism of supply chain finance on corporate green technological innovation from the perspective of financing optimization, by employing the two way fixed effect model and the mediation effect model. The empirical results show that: ① Supply chain finance significantly improves the level of enterprises’ green technological innovation, and this conclusion remains valid after a series of robustness tests; ② Supply chain finance affects corporate green technological innovation by alleviating financing constraints, empowering enterprises’ digital transformation, controlling risk fluctuations, and improving carbon information disclosure; ③ The driving effect of supply chain finance on green technological innovation is more pronounced for firms in the growth stage, technology intensive enterprises and labor intensive enterprises. The research conclusions offer scientific empirical evidence and decision making references for guiding enterprises’ green innovation development via supply chain financing, provide a basis for governments to formulate relevant policies, and promote the improvement of the green financial system and the advancement of green innovation.

title: Unmasking Fraudulent Financial Statements in Banks: The Interplay of Greenwashing, Political Connection, and Board Independence
summary: Purpose: The study investigates the relationship between greenwashing, political connections, and fraudulent financial statements in the Indonesian banking sector, with independent commissioners serving as a moderating variable. Methods/Stu
content: Purpose: The study investigates the relationship between greenwashing, political connections, and fraudulent financial statements in the Indonesian banking sector, with independent commissioners serving as a moderating variable. Methods/Study design/Approach: The study uses panel data from 434 bank-year observations of Indonesian commercial banks during 2016–2022. Fraud is measured using the F-Score and Beneish M-Score models, while the hypotheses are tested using panel regression and moderation analysis. Result/Findings: The results show that greenwashing is significantly associated with fraudulent financial reporting, generally negatively across models. Political connections also significantly affect fraudulent financial statement, although the direction varies by measurement approach. Independent commissioners moderate the relationship between greenwashing and fraud, but their role in the political connections-fraud relationship is limited. Analysis comparing pre-crisis and COVID-19 periods shows that economic stress influences these relationships. Findings have practical implications for banking governance by emphasizing effective board oversight, stronger monitoring by independent commissioners, and improved transparency in sustainability and political-related disclosures to reducing fraud. Novelty/Originality/Value: The study contributes to the literature by Employing both F-Score and M-Score models and comparing pre-crisis and COVID-19 periods, the study shows that economic stress and ESG scrutiny alter governance effectiveness and incentives for fraudulent reporting in emerging-market banks.

title: Prediction of Type 2 Diabetes using genomics and proteomics: the HUNT Study
summary: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is a multifactorial metabolic disorder with an increasing global prevalence and significant health burdens. Early identification of individuals at high risk is crucial for timely intervention and prevention of T2D and
content: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is a multifactorial metabolic disorder with an increasing global prevalence and significant health burdens. Early identification of individuals at high risk is crucial for timely intervention and prevention of T2D and complications. This study aims to investigate the association between the blood plasma proteome and T2D, identify protein biomarkers associated with incident T2D, and explore the underlying biological pathways involved in the disease development in the Trondelag Health Study (HUNT). The HUNT Study is a population-based cohort with four waves of enrolment beginning in 1984. Samples from HUNT3 were analysed with SomaScan including 3,221 using SomaScanv4.0 (HUNT-Soma5k, ~5,000 proteins) and 2,181 on SomaScanv4.1 (HUNT-Soma7k, ~7,000 proteins). We performed logistic regression and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) to generate the protein risk scores, and gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) to identify potential biological pathways for incident T2D. We identified 313 (308 proteins) and 142 (128 proteins) aptamers that are significantly associated with incident T2D, in HUNT-Soma5k and HUNT-Soma7k, respectively. In HUNT-Soma5k, MXRA8 has strongest association with decreased risk and PLXB2 has strongest association with increased risk; while IGFBP2 has strongest association with decreased risk and INHBC has strongest association with increased risk for incident T2D in HUNT-Soma7k. The most significant pathway from GO Biological Process is organic acid metabolic process in both datasets. The associated proteins and biological pathways identified represent insights into the underlying molecular mechanism of T2D and may serve as potential biomarkers for risk prediction and prevention for T2D.

title: The Health Coverage and the Social Inequity for Kidney Failure Patients in Morocco: A Glance at Haemodialysis Centres, Fez/Morocco
summary: Introduction: This study aims to reveal to which extend the health coverage new regime (AMO) is crucial for kidneys failure patients and for any other patient, it covers the majority of their medical activities like the haemodialysis sessio
content: Introduction: This study aims to reveal to which extend the health coverage new regime (AMO) is crucial for kidneys failure patients and for any other patient, it covers the majority of their medical activities like the haemodialysis sessions (3 times a week), the different injections, the symptomatic treatment, etc. the new regime was established by the government to reduce disparities between citizens and to allow their easy access to health services even in public or private sector. Methods: This study analyzed 60 patients with kidney failure disease after surveying them. We used Google Forms for collecting Data and Microsoft Excel for creating Graphs. Results: Of the total participants, 56.6% of patients were females, while 43.3% of them were males. All the respondents had chronic kidney failure (100%. There were 72.9% unemployed, 13.6% working, 3.4% students, and 1.7% retired. More than 74% belong to Compulsory health insurance (AMO), which allows patients to benefit free of charge from the panel offered to kidney failure patients, replacing the ancient regime RAMED. When the rights to health care ended, 53.6% of cases went to court, and only 33.9% could pay temporarily. Discussion: This study indicates that patients are enormously satisfied and feel dignity in their lives; that is to say, that health coverage reduces disparities between Moroccan citizens, in this case, kidney failure patients, by allowing them to have access to all health services, either in the public sector or in the private one. Nevertheless, when the rights of health coverage end, they are kicked out of private hemodialysis centers to the public ones, which impose billing as well.

title: Source‐Unbiased Subsurface Monitoring With Seismic Noise
summary: Abstract This study addresses a key limitation of seismic noise interferometry for subsurface monitoring: the impact of non‐stationary sources on seismic velocity change estimates. Conventional methods rely on time‐period references, which
content: Abstract This study addresses a key limitation of seismic noise interferometry for subsurface monitoring: the impact of non‐stationary sources on seismic velocity change estimates. Conventional methods rely on time‐period references, which can inherit source‐related effects when source conditions vary, biasing the estimated velocity changes. This is particularly relevant in urban and industrial environments, where quasi‐monochromatic sources are often present. We show that frequency variations in such signals can produce apparent seismic velocity changes of equivalent magnitude through analytical and numerical analyses. To address this issue, we introduce REFTION, a spatial‐reference approach based on synchronous comparison of correlation functions across seismic stations. We demonstrate its performance in an active open‐pit mine, successfully monitoring a tailings dam under complex noise conditions. By reducing sensitivity to source variability, REFTION enables reliable subsurface monitoring in challenging environments, where anthropogenic noise can be transformed into a valuable monitoring tool.

title: Epigenetic signatures of attention problems in youth with childhood exposure to family and community violence
summary: AIM: The link between violence-related epigenetic changes and attentional problems (APs) is still not well understood. This article examines if exposure to family and community violence during childhood and adolescence may shape DNA methyla
content: AIM: The link between violence-related epigenetic changes and attentional problems (APs) is still not well understood. This article examines if exposure to family and community violence during childhood and adolescence may shape DNA methylation patterns associated with attention in youth. METHOD: This study used data from a longitudinal cohort with 500 first-grade Brazilian students. The following measures were investigated: attention problems, family violence, and community violence. Mann-Whitney-U and Kruskal-Wallis were used to identify group differences and Spearman correlation to access variables associations. Top 1% CpGs were overlapped. Epigenetics analyses were performed using Epigenome-wide association study (EWAS, 850K) and Prediction Analysis of Microarray (PAM). Linear regression models were applied to candidate genes analyses. All models used significance level at 5%. RESULTS: AP was correlated to three types of violence (family, psychological family, and community violence). EWAS and PAM identified five genes in common: SLC43A2, SMN1/2, TPO, DTNA, and CLMN, collectively implicating neurodevelopmental, cellular homeostatic, and endocrine mechanisms. PAM successfully predicted attention problems (AP) in two models (AP alone and AP combined with physical violence). Among the selected genes, several were related to neurodevelopment and neuronal maintenance (SMN1/2, MYT1L); structural organization (DTNA, CLMN); and cellular signaling (DTNA) functions; and immune, metabolic, and endocrine responses (SLC43A2, TPO). These alterations were associated with attention problems and exposure to family and community violence. CONCLUSION: Early-life violence is biologically embedded through epigenetic modifications affecting attention, pointing to a complex interplay between environmental adversity and gene regulation. Integrative prevention strategies targeting psychosocial/molecular pathways of vulnerability are needed.

title: Performance-measurement systems as actors and boundary objects: a sociomaterial perspective to the provision of prison services
summary: The paper explores the performance-measurement systems (PMSs) used in the provision of prison services (and their non-human agent role) to reflect on: the role PMSs play in inter-organisational relationships; the boundary objects that conne
content: The paper explores the performance-measurement systems (PMSs) used in the provision of prison services (and their non-human agent role) to reflect on: the role PMSs play in inter-organisational relationships; the boundary objects that connect human and non-human actors across inter-organisational levels; and what affordances such connections generate. The study focuses on the English prison sector, drawing on document analysis and interviews. The findings show that PMSs represent both active non-human agents and boundary objects. The positioning of the actors involved can be seen as a second-order boundary object. Moreover, PMSs can generate affordances that go beyond the initially-intended purposes.

title: Soil chemical properties of smallholder avocado intercropping systems in northern Tanzania
summary: Avocado production is expanding in northern Tanzania; however, information on the spatial variability of soil fertility across major production areas remains limited. This study assessed soil chemical properties in smallholder avocado agrof
content: Avocado production is expanding in northern Tanzania; however, information on the spatial variability of soil fertility across major production areas remains limited. This study assessed soil chemical properties in smallholder avocado agroforestry systems across six districts in the Tanga, Kilimanjaro, and Arusha regions. Composite soil samples (0–30 cm depth) were collected from 54 villages and analysed for pH, electrical conductivity (EC), organic carbon (OC), total nitrogen (TN), available phosphorus (P), exchangeable potassium (K), calcium (Ca), magnesium (Mg), and copper (Cu). District-level differences were evaluated using one-way analysis of variance, while Pearson correlation, principal component analysis (PCA), and linear mixed-effects models were used to examine nutrient relationships, spatial fertility patterns, and associations with elevation. Soils across all districts were non-saline (EC: 0.13–0.25 dS m −1 ), and pH values (5.9–6.7) fell within the range generally considered suitable for avocado cultivation. Meru and Karatu generally exhibited higher concentrations of OC, TN, and exchangeable base cations. In contrast, Lushoto, Korogwe, and Rombo showed lower concentrations of some nutrients, particularly K and P. Elevated Cu concentrations were observed in Moshi and may be associated with the long-term use of copper-based fungicides. The linear mixed-effects model indicated that only OC and TN increased significantly with elevation. PCA showed that inter-district variation in soil fertility was primarily associated with differences in exchangeable base cations and organic matter-related nutrients. These findings provide baseline information on soil fertility patterns in northern Tanzania and a foundation for future studies integrating soil properties with topographic, climatic, and management factors to support sustainable avocado production.

title: Seasonality and functional traits of periphytic algae shape zooperiphyton colonization
summary: Abstract We investigated the influence of seasonality and the phycoperiphyton on the colonization dynamics of zooperiphyton on artificial polyethylene terephthalate substrates in a tropical hypereutrophic reservoir. We tested the hypothesis
content: Abstract We investigated the influence of seasonality and the phycoperiphyton on the colonization dynamics of zooperiphyton on artificial polyethylene terephthalate substrates in a tropical hypereutrophic reservoir. We tested the hypothesis that seasonal climatic conditions drive changes in zooperiphyton colonization and successional trajectories, with stronger effects on functional aspects of the community. In situ colonization studies lasting 28 days were conducted during two seasons. Substrates were sampled, and associated phycoperiphyton and zooperiphyton communities were identified and quantified, while environmental variables were measured to characterize the environment. Structural equation models were used to determine the effects of the phycoperiphyton on zooperiphyton. The zooperiphyton assemblage was composed of rotifers, ciliates, testate amoebae, insects, and nematodes. Rotifers exhibited the highest species richness, while ciliates dominated the community structure throughout both seasons. Epistylis plicatilis was the primary colonizer after 3 h in both seasons. Successional processes progressed more rapidly during the dry season, likely due to more stable, favorable abiotic conditions. In the rainy season, high rainfall and stalked algae influenced the zooperiphyton community. Furthermore, prostrate, stalked, and entangled algae influenced herbivores and predators. Our findings demonstrate that seasonal disturbances, such as rainfall, mediate the interactions between phycoperiphyton and zooperiphyton, thereby shaping the biofilm’s successional trajectory.

title: Influence of Corporate Strategies on Institutional Performance of Public Universities in Nyanza Region, Kenya
source: International Journal of Social Science and Humanities Research (IJSSHR) ISSN 2959-7056 (o) 2959-7048 (p)
summary: Kenyan public universities face numerous challenges, including declining government capitation, mounting debt, intense competition for students and low research visibility, which highlight the need for strong corporate strategies to ensure
content: Kenyan public universities face numerous challenges, including declining government capitation, mounting debt, intense competition for students and low research visibility, which highlight the need for strong corporate strategies to ensure better performance and long-term viability. This study aimed at investigating the influence of corporate strategies on the institutional performance of public universities in the Nyanza region, Kenya. The specific objectives were to examine the influence of growth strategies, assess the influence of competitive strategies, and analyse the influence of cooperative strategies on the institutional performance of public universities in Nyanza region, Kenya. The study was anchored on the Ansoff Matrix, Michael Porter’s Generic Competitive Strategies model and the Resource-Based View Theory. A correlational cross-sectional survey research design was used, targeting 85 members of university management boards, deans and directors in four public universities in the Nyanza region: Kisii University, Maseno University, Jaramogi Oginga Odinga University of Science and Technology (JOOUST) and Tom Mboya University. Using the formula of Yamane (1967), a sample size of 70 respondents was selected through stratified random sampling with Neyman proportional allocation across the three management strata. Data were collected using structured questionnaires with a five-point Likert scale and piloted at Rongo University with 30 respondents. Descriptive statistics (means, standard deviations) and inferential statistics (Pearson correlation and multiple linear regression analysis) were computed using the Statistical Package for Social Sciences (SPSS), and results were presented in tables. The study found that growth strategies strongly predict institutional performance (B=0.422; β=0.355; p=.000), followed by competitive strategies (B=0.368; β=0.308; p=.000) and cooperative strategies (B=0.338; β=0.282; p=.000), with the three strategies jointly explaining 62.7% of the variance in institutional performance. All predictors positively influence performance, confirming their significant contributions. The study concluded that growth strategies have the greatest positive impact on institutional performance, with diversification through digital platforms and online programmes as the highest-rated items; competitive strategies enhance performance chiefly through differentiation and a student-centred focus, while cost-efficiency measures remain the weakest lever; and cooperative strategies contribute through strategic alliances, co-marketing and shared-resource networks, though their direct contribution to financial sustainability is perceived as moderate. The study therefore recommended that public universities in Nyanza leverage more growth strategies, particularly online and market-oriented programmes; intensify cost-efficiency measures to attain financial stability; strengthen networks for resource sharing, outreach and joint branding; and

title: Integrated Genome Mining and Bioactivity-Guided Isolation of Antimicrobial Peptides from Bacillus amyloliquefaciens BS4
summary: Bacterial resistance remains a critical global health challenge, driving the continuous search for novel antimicrobial agents. Bacillus amyloliquefaciens is a recognized repository of bioactive metabolites; however, its full biosynthetic po
content: Bacterial resistance remains a critical global health challenge, driving the continuous search for novel antimicrobial agents. Bacillus amyloliquefaciens is a recognized repository of bioactive metabolites; however, its full biosynthetic potential requires integrated genomic and experimental validation. This study characterized the antimicrobial profile of B. amyloliquefaciens BS4 through a hybrid pipeline. Genome sequencing and de novo assembly revealed a 3.9 Mb chromosome with a G + C content of 46.14%. Functional annotation identified 3,887 coding sequences, including pathways for siderophore biosynthesis and a complete bacilysin biosynthetic cluster. BGC analysis using antiSMASH v7.1.0 and BAGEL4 identified 18 biosynthetic gene clusters, while similarity network analysis via BiG-SCAPE highlighted unique singleton BGCs, indicating untapped biosynthetic diversity. Although in silico screening via Macrel predicted two putative cationic antimicrobial peptides (AMPs), bioactivity-guided purification utilizing sequential RP-HPLC, and de novo sequencing revealed a distinct set of four active peptides. Notably, three of these sequences were identified as fragments derived from the BclA exosporium protein family, highlighting the structural proteome as a non-canonical source of antimicrobials. The purified fractions exhibited activity against M. luteus and E. coli, while displaying no significant hemolytic activity or cytotoxicity, even above the MIC values. Molecular docking further supported the interaction of these candidates with bacterial targets. Overall, this hybrid strategy effectively uncovers the antimicrobial complexity of BS4, revealing 'cryptic' peptide candidates with therapeutic potential.

title: Assessing the nexus between food insecurity and economic shocks: Evidence from agricultural households in north-east Nigeria
summary: Food insecurity remains a significant global problem, particularly in low-income countries, where households are consistently exposed to economic shocks. These economic disruptions reduce the productivity of farm families, exacerbating thei
content: Food insecurity remains a significant global problem, particularly in low-income countries, where households are consistently exposed to economic shocks. These economic disruptions reduce the productivity of farm families, exacerbating their food insecurity. This research analysed the nexus between economic shocks and food insecurity of agricultural households in northeastern Nigeria. Notably, conflict has severely disrupted food systems in northeastern Nigeria. The study utilised the 2019 Nigeria Living Standards Survey (NLSS). Food insecurity and the influence of economic shocks on it were measured using the Food Insecurity Experience Scale (FIES) and an Ordered Probit regression, respectively. The food insecurity status of the households revealed that 78% of the families were suffering from various degrees of food insecurity. The regression analysis revealed that economic stressors have a positive influence on food insecurity . The study shows heightened vulnerability of agricultural households to food poverty amid economic disruptions. This study recommends that the government and other stakeholders in the food system implement targeted initiatives to strengthen household resilience against economic stressors, thereby reducing food insecurity among agricultural households in Northeast Nigeria.

title: A diagnostic framework blue-green infrastructure readiness in developing-country cities
summary: Climate change is intensifying floods and other water-related hazards, exposing the limits of conventional grey infrastructure in developing-country cities. Blue-Green Infrastructure (BGI) offers a promising adaptation pathway, but its impl
content: Climate change is intensifying floods and other water-related hazards, exposing the limits of conventional grey infrastructure in developing-country cities. Blue-Green Infrastructure (BGI) offers a promising adaptation pathway, but its implementation depends on more than technical suitability. In many resource-constrained municipalities, BGI uptake is limited by fragmented governance, unstable financing, weak technical capacity, and limited public legitimacy. The Blue-Green Infrastructure Diagnostic Tool (BGIDT) assesses these enabling conditions before large-scale implementation. The tool evaluates readiness across four interdependent domains: policy and governance, economic and financial capacity, technical and environmental capacity, and social and cultural legitimacy. Applied to three Colombian municipalities representing high, moderate, and low institutional capacity, the BGIDT shows that readiness depends on the alignment of governance, finance, technical systems, and social legitimacy. Medellín demonstrates how coordinated metropolitan governance reinforces financial, technical, and social capacity. Neiva and Pitalito illustrate how fragmented authority and unstable resources constrain implementation despite policy support. The BGIDT provides municipalities, funders, and policymakers with a practical framework to identify implementation gaps, prioritise capacity-building, target investment, and monitor readiness over time.

title: Квантовий маркетинг в електронній комерції
summary: Високі темпи цифровізації бізнесу посилили потребу у складних маркетингових механізмах, здатних формувати виважені, визначені та контекстуальні процедури прийняття рішень споживачами. Традиційні лінійні маркетингові моделі дедалі менш ефект
content: Високі темпи цифровізації бізнесу посилили потребу у складних маркетингових механізмах, здатних формувати виважені, визначені та контекстуальні процедури прийняття рішень споживачами. Традиційні лінійні маркетингові моделі дедалі менш ефективні, враховуючи динаміку поведінки в алгоритмічно опосеред­кованому та інформаційно насиченому цифро­вому світі. Емпірична прогалина, яку врахо­вувано в цьому дослідженні, повʼязана з економічною та поведінковою ефективністю квантових маркетингових механізмів в елект­ронній комерції. Дослідження ґрунтується на гіпотезі, що підвищення інтенсивності кван­тового маркетингу в електронній комерції має позитивний, але нелінійний вплив на економічні результати компаній, які опосередковуються змінами споживчої поведінки та посилюються в умовах ринкової невизначеності. Визначено, якою мірою інтенсивність квантового марке­тингу впливає на купівельну поведінку спожи­вачів та ефективність компанії як нелінійним, так і інтерактивним, а також залежним від стану способом. Використано багато­націо­нальну панельну модель компаній електронної комерції за 2020 та 2024 рр. Створено загальний індекс інтенсивності квантового маркетингу для відображення глибини персона­лізації, адаптивності в режимі реального часу, координації між каналами та інтенсивності експериментів. Вони використовують панельні економетричні моделі з фіксованими ефектами, що включають поведінкове посередництво, нелінійні специфікації та умови взаємодії для позначення контекстуальної волатильності. Статистичні результати показують, що інтенсивність квантового маркетингу має пози­тивний та статистично значущий вплив на коефіцієнт конверсії, дохід на відвідувача, валовий прибуток та довічну цінність клієнта. Дані свідчать про зниження граничної прибутковості, що підтверджує нелінійний характер дії передових маркетингових меха­нізмів. Отримані результати також демонструють, що економічні ефекти реалі­зуються через поведінкові змінні, які відобра­жають вплив певної специфіки та сукупно пояснюють приблизно від чверті до третини всіх ефектів. Синергія ефектів між цифровими каналами є позитивною, і важливо відзначити необхідність синхронізованих омніканальних стратегій. Волатильність ринку підвищує ефективність застосування квантового марке­тингу, особливо за умов зростаючої невизна­ченості, що підтверджує гіпотезу контекстної залежності. Дослідження показує, що його ефективність була максимальною у 2022 р., а згодом стабілізувалася, у міру того як ринки ставали більш зрілими, а споживачі більш адаптованими. Загалом дослідження робить науковий внесок, демонструючи квантифікацію маркетингу як кількісно вимірюваного еконо­мет­ричного підходу та можливості його інтеграції з інструментарієм поведінкової економіки і панельного економетричного аналізу. Отримані результати створюють основу для подальших досліджень квантового маркетингу в електронній комерції, зокрема для аналізу клієнтських даних, застосування експе­риментальних алгоритмів у цифрових каналах збуту

title: Impact of EAAT2 Dysfunction on AMPA/NMDA-Mediated Excitability in Neuronal Activity
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Introduction Epilepsy is among the most prevalent neurological disorders. The astrocytic excitatory amino acid transporter (EAAT2) plays a key role in regulating excitability, by controlling extracellular glutamate levels and glutamate rece
content: Introduction Epilepsy is among the most prevalent neurological disorders. The astrocytic excitatory amino acid transporter (EAAT2) plays a key role in regulating excitability, by controlling extracellular glutamate levels and glutamate receptor activation [1,2]. Reduced EAAT2 expression has been reported in several epilepsy patients [1,3]. However, the impact of neuron-astrocyte interactions on hyperexcitability on single cell level is underexplored. We developed a biophysical model of a presynaptic neuron and astrocyte to explore the relation between astrocytic EAAT2-mediated glutamate clearance, presynaptic glutamate receptors and bursting activity. Methods We build on our previous work [4,5], where we consider a presynaptic neuron and an astrocyte in a finite extracellular space (ECS). This model describes sodium, potassium, chloride dynamics as well as calcium-dependent exocytosis and glutamate-glutamine (GG) recycling. For this study, we add a potassium bath with diffusion to the ECS to induce neuronal bursting (Fig. 1A). Additionally, we implement the presynaptic glutamate receptors AMPA and NMDA, which are important in regulating hyperexcitability. Lastly, we study the impact of the antiseizure drugs perampanel and memantine by simulating the effect of these AMPA and NMDA receptor antagonists. Results We induce neuronal bursting by increasing extracellular potassium in the bath. We first examine how AMPA and NMDA permeabilities affect burst frequency (Fig. 1C), where frequency refers to spike frequency during the last burst or during tonic firing, to fit the NMDA/AMPA ratio to experimental data [6]. Higher permeabilities increase neuronal firing and intracellular calcium, triggering a feedback loop that enhances neuronal glutamate release. Reducing EAAT permeability raises burst frequency and induces tonic firing (Fig. 1B). Finally, AMPA and NMDA antagonists, perampanel and memantine [7], reduce firing despite elevated extracellular glutamate, with perampanel showing a more significant reduction in firing frequency (Fig. 1D). Discussion Our results show that reduced EAAT expression, as observed in several epilepsy patients, results in increased extracellular glutamate and overstimulation of excitatory glutamate receptors. Furthermore, we show that the AMPA and NMDA receptor permeabilities affect burst frequency. Receptor antagonists such as perampanel and memantine are able to reduce firing. In conclusion, our detailed neuron–astrocyte model provides insight into the effects of reduced EAAT expression and receptor antagonists on hyperexcitability. GG, HS, and JH were supported by the ERDF-Project Brain dynamics, No. CZ.02.01.01/00/22_008/0004643, a Lumina-Quaeruntur fellowship (LQ100302301), and the long-term strategic development financing of the Institute of Computer Science (RVO:67985807). title: POST-OCCUPANCY EVALUATION OF OFFICE BUILDINGS IN LAGOS: IMPLICATIONS FOR FACILITY MANAGEMENT
source: International Journal of Built Environment and Earth Science
summary: This paper investigates the post-occupancy evaluation of office buildings in Lagos, Nigeria, and its implications for facility management practice. The commercial real estate sector in Lagos has expanded rapidly, resulting in a large stock
content: This paper investigates the post-occupancy evaluation of office buildings in Lagos, Nigeria, and its implications for facility management practice. The commercial real estate sector in Lagos has expanded rapidly, resulting in a large stock of office buildings. However, recent evidence indicates that most occupants are dissatisfied with the facilities, largely due to design inefficiencies and poor facility management. Hence, this research explores the impact of building design and management practices on occupant satisfaction through an extensive literature review. The article reviews the literature and summarizes findings from studies conducted in the Nigerian commercial office environment on post-occupancy evaluation methodologies, indoor environmental quality (IEQ) parameters, and facility management practices. The study states that the key environmental factors of quality (EIQ) that can significantly influence occupant satisfaction include natural lighting, ventilation, thermal comfort, and spatial layout. Some of the major challenges include a lack of financial support for maintenance, a shortage of technical skills, weak policy structures, and other local factors specific to Lagos, such as power outages and a tropical climate. The article suggests a number of ways to make changes, such as making post-occupancy evaluation routine, upgrading facility management practices, applying user-centered design principles, adopting context-specific management approaches, and expanding regulatory control. The research finds that a comprehensive approach combining building design, management, and regular assessment is necessary for the attainment of sustainable building performance and occupant satisfaction in the Lagos commercial office sector.

title: Sustainable Agro-Food Systems in the Digital Era: A Systematic Review of Economic, Technological, and Managerial Perspectives
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This dataset supports the systematic review article "Sustainable Agro-Food Systems in the Digital Era: A Systematic Review of Economic, Technological, and Managerial Perspectives", which synthesises evidence from sixteen (16) studies examin
content: This dataset supports the systematic review article "Sustainable Agro-Food Systems in the Digital Era: A Systematic Review of Economic, Technological, and Managerial Perspectives", which synthesises evidence from sixteen (16) studies examining how economic instruments, technological innovations, and managerial governance mechanisms interact synergistically to shape sustainable outcomes in agro-food systems. The review covers multiple thematic dimensions including economic instruments and policies (environmental protection taxes, supply chain finance, green credit lines, bioeconomy and ESG strategies), technological innovations (artificial intelligence, machine learning, remote sensing, Internet of Things, unmanned aerial vehicles, blockchain, quantum machine learning, multi-agent reinforcement learning, and generative artificial intelligence), and managerial and governance factors (economies of scale, government regulation, institutional support, stakeholder engagement, data governance, and farmer trust). The included studies span diverse geographic contexts, including Asia (China, India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, Sri Lanka), Europe (Spain, Ireland, the Netherlands, Germany, United Kingdom), South Asia, and global datasets (FAO, NASA POWER). The dataset includes Figure 1 (PRISMA 2020 Flow Diagram illustrating the study selection process from initial database search to 16 included studies), Supplementary Document 1 (PRISMA 2020 Checklist with 27 items completed for the systematic review), Supplementary Document 2 (Risk of Bias Assessment Criteria detailing the quality appraisal framework adapted for diverse study designs spanning empirical quantitative studies, qualitative case studies, systematic reviews, narrative reviews, Delphi consultations, and simulation-based research), Supplementary Document 3 (Full Data Extraction Form containing standardised data from all sixteen included studies including author(s), year, geographic scope, study design, sectoral focus, key technologies investigated, economic instruments and policies examined, managerial and governance factors considered, quantitative findings, and risk of bias assessment). All files are available under a Creative Commons Zero (CC0 1.0) license.

title: Forensic Accounting Techniques and Fraud Detection in Selected Public Entities in Nigeria
source: JOURNAL OF BUSINESS AND AFRICAN ECONOMY
summary: The increasing sophistication and frequency of fraudulent activities have created a greater need for effective mechanisms to detect and address financial irregularities. This sets the foundation for this study, which evaluated the effect of
content: The increasing sophistication and frequency of fraudulent activities have created a greater need for effective mechanisms to detect and address financial irregularities. This sets the foundation for this study, which evaluated the effect of forensic accounting techniques in detecting fraud within the Nigerian public sector. This study employed survey research design, and population comprised 357 staff members with accounting related functions of the 3 selected Nigerian public entities (Federal Ministry of Finance, Federal Ministry of Budget and Financial Planning, and Economic and Financial Crimes Commission). This study employed a purposive sampling technique to select a sample size of 240 and data obtained through close ended questionnaire was analysed using partial least square through the aid of SMARTPLS. The regression analysis revealed that all three techniques; Benford Law, computer-assisted auditing tools (CAATs), and data mining analytics have positive and significant effects on fraud detection, demonstrating their usefulness in identifying financial anomalies and irregularities. The study concludes that forensic accounting techniques such as Benford Law, CAATs, and data mining analytics are powerful tools that significantly improve fraud detection in Nigerian public sector entities. These techniques provide systematic approaches for identifying financial anomalies, thereby enhancing accountability and transparency within public institutions. Based on the findings, it is recommended that Nigerian public sector entities adopt and integrate these forensic accounting techniques into their financial monitoring and auditing processes.

title: МЕХАНІЗМИ ВПЛИВУ ФІНАНСОВИХ ТЕХНОЛОГІЙ НА МІНІМІЗАЦІЮ КОРУПЦІЙНИХ РИЗИКІВ У ФІНАНСОВІЙ СИСТЕМІ: ЦИФРОВІ ІНСТРУМЕНТИ, МОЖЛИВОСТІ ТА ПЕРСПЕКТИВИ
source: Європейський науковий журнал Економічних та Фінансових інновацій
summary: У статті досліджено механізми впливу фінансових технологій на мінімізацію корупційних ризиків у сучасній фінансовій системі та визначено можливості використання цифрових інструментів для підвищення її прозорості, підзвітності та контрольова
content: У статті досліджено механізми впливу фінансових технологій на мінімізацію корупційних ризиків у сучасній фінансовій системі та визначено можливості використання цифрових інструментів для підвищення її прозорості, підзвітності та контрольованості. Актуальність дослідження зумовлена стрімкою цифровою трансформацією фінансового сектору, поширенням цифрових платежів, онлайн-банкінгу, блокчейн-технологій, штучного інтелекту, аналізу великих даних та цифрової ідентифікації, які суттєво змінюють механізми здійснення, моніторингу та контролю фінансових операцій. Метою статті є дослідження механізмів впливу фінансових технологій на мінімізацію корупційних ризиків у фінансовій системі, систематизація основних цифрових інструментів, здатних забезпечувати прозорість і простежуваність фінансових операцій, автоматизацію контрольних процедур та виявлення потенційно корупційних практик, а також визначення ключових можливостей, обмежень і перспектив їх подальшого застосування. Методологічну основу дослідження становлять методи аналізу та синтезу, систематизації та узагальнення наукових підходів, порівняльного аналізу, бібліометричного аналізу та логічного узагальнення. Здійснено огляд сучасних наукових досліджень щодо впливу FinTech на трансформацію фінансової системи, фінансову інклюзію, ефективність банків, фінансову прозорість і підзвітність. Систематизовано ключові цифрові інструменти, які можуть використовуватися для мінімізації корупційних ризиків, зокрема цифрові платежі, блокчейн, штучний інтелект, великі дані, цифрову ідентифікацію та автоматизований фінансовий моніторинг. Обґрунтовано, що основними механізмами їх антикорупційного впливу є формування цифрового сліду фінансових операцій, зменшення інформаційної асиметрії, підвищення прозорості фінансових потоків, автоматизація контрольних процедур, своєчасне виявлення аномальних операцій та зниження можливостей для ручного втручання у фінансові процеси. Водночас визначено, що цифровізація не забезпечує автоматичного зниження корупційних ризиків, оскільки ефективність фінтех значною мірою залежить від якості інституційного середовища, нормативно-правового регулювання, захисту даних, цифрової компетентності персоналу та спроможності контролюючих органів реагувати на виявлені ризики. Запропоновано розглядати фінтех не як окремий технологічний інструмент, а як складову інтегрованої цифрової екосистеми фінансової прозорості та антикорупційного контролю.

title: From Coase to culture? Visible Hands Build Equilibria
summary: Abstract This essay proposes that the classic distinction in Ronald Coase's 1937 paper ‘The nature of the firm’ ( Economica , vol. 4, pp. 386–405) between firms and markets be gracefully retired, having been duly celebrated for its field‐la
content: Abstract This essay proposes that the classic distinction in Ronald Coase's 1937 paper ‘The nature of the firm’ ( Economica , vol. 4, pp. 386–405) between firms and markets be gracefully retired, having been duly celebrated for its field‐launching contribution to organizational economics. Some of the reasons for retiring this famous distinction rely on other insights from that seminal paper. In this sense, this essay offers an updated appreciation of Coase's paper. In addition, escaping this classic distinction motivates two agendas for organizational economics: (i) a redoubling of research on economic interactions that are organized but not within a single organization; and (ii) a ‘coalitional’ reconception of Coase's ‘conscious power’ of the entrepreneur that applies to the management of economic interactions not only within organizations but also between them. Both agendas seem likely to require new thinking about how parties build equilibria, so I close the essay by suggesting topics from the analysis of organizational culture that might inspire models of building equilibria.

title: Unlocking green growth: the role of Fintech development in promoting economic sustainability
summary: Despite the global problem of environmental degradation, and the regulatory initiatives being driven by international and governmental bodies to ensure that organizations adhere to sustainable development goals, there are still gaps that re
content: Despite the global problem of environmental degradation, and the regulatory initiatives being driven by international and governmental bodies to ensure that organizations adhere to sustainable development goals, there are still gaps that require further research. Therefore, this research aims to fill the gap in the economic sustainability literature by analyzing the association of Fintech development with economic sustainability through green finance, environmental benefits, and natural resource management, as well as sequential mediation analysis, conceptually integrated under the umbrella of the Natural-Resource-Based View (NRBV). The study identified companies that met the criteria for the phenomenon in all three countries: Romania, Mexico and Spain. Structural equation modelling (SEM) was used for data analysis. The results show that Fintech development is directly and significantly associated with economic sustainability and a strong association of green financing. In turn, green finance generates considerable environmental benefits, which contribute to sustainable economic performance, and natural resource management positively influences economic sustainability, confirming its essential role in the transition to sustainable economic models. The results of this study are valuable to government authorities and business executives who make decisions about promoting sustainability, and provides managerial recommendations on investments in Fintech technologies, green instruments, and responsible resource use practices.

title: Du management des frontières au récit d’une Europe solidaire
summary: Depuis les années 2000, les politiques migratoires européennes sont orientées par le management migratoire. Alors que ce dernier se présente comme une pure administration technique des flux migratoires, il ne peut neutraliser sa charge poli
content: Depuis les années 2000, les politiques migratoires européennes sont orientées par le management migratoire. Alors que ce dernier se présente comme une pure administration technique des flux migratoires, il ne peut neutraliser sa charge politique, liée au récit impérial historiquement fabriqué par l’Europe. Les enquêtes menées aux frontières orientales et septentrionales de l’Union Européenne dans le cadre d’une philosophie de terrain permettent de comprendre comment la doctrine du management migratoire s’est constituée en rhétorique accompagnant et invisibilisant des politiques migratoires répressives et violentes. Cette euphémisation va de pair avec la construction du récit d’une Europe vertueuse, tournant l’attention vers une gestion humanitaire des migrations qui alimente la représentation d’une Europe solidaire.

title: Sustainable Logistics Management Practices and Performance of the Distribution Firm Industry in Kenya.
source: International Journal of Social Science and Humanities Research (IJSSHR)
summary: Sustainable logistics management practices have become a key driver of performance in the distribution industry as firms face increasing pressure to reduce environmental impact while remaining competitive amid rising operational costs, regu
content: Sustainable logistics management practices have become a key driver of performance in the distribution industry as firms face increasing pressure to reduce environmental impact while remaining competitive amid rising operational costs, regulatory requirements and growing consumer awareness. However, many distribution firms in Kenya continue to rely on outdated transportation systems, inefficient warehousing and non-compliant waste disposal methods, which raise fuel costs, delay deliveries and weaken customer satisfaction. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to establish the effect of sustainable logistics management practices on the performance of the distribution firm industry in Kenya. It specifically examined the effect of sustainable transportation, sustainable packaging, sustainable inventory management and sustainable reverse logistics on performance. The study was anchored on the Resource-Based View, Triple Bottom Line Theory, Systems Theory and Closed-Loop Supply Chain Theory. A cross-sectional survey design was adopted, targeting 234 logistics mapping officers, dispatch officers, programme coordinators and supervisors in 26 distribution firms operating in Nairobi, Mombasa and Kisumu. A sample of 148 respondents was determined using the Yamane formula and selected through stratified random sampling. Data were collected using a semi-structured questionnaire and analysed using descriptive statistics, Structural Equation Modelling in AMOS and content analysis in NVIVO, and the results were presented in tables and discussed. The findings revealed that sustainable transportation had a positive and significant effect on performance, explaining 70.3% of its variation. The study also found that sustainable inventory management had a strong positive and significant effect on performance, explaining 69.0% of its variation. The study further found that sustainable packaging had a positive and significant effect on performance, driven by biodegradable and renewable materials rather than packaging weight reduction. Finally, the study established that sustainable reverse logistics had a moderate but significant effect on performance, driven mainly by reuse and recycling, while the four practices jointly explained 93.1% of the variation in performance. The study, therefore, recommends that distribution firms should adopt low-emission vehicles, route optimization and backhauling, invest in demand forecasting, inventory turnover optimization and eco-friendly warehousing, prioritize biodegradable and renewable packaging, and strengthen reuse, recycling and take-back schemes through collaboration with suppliers, recyclers and supportive government policies.

title: A Development Strategy for an Age of Polycrisis
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: The monograph argues that the Global South has entered a structural break in its development trajectory, driven by an interlocking polycrisis of climate extremes, sovereign debt distress, geoeconomic fragmentation, and rapid AI-driven labor
content: The monograph argues that the Global South has entered a structural break in its development trajectory, driven by an interlocking polycrisis of climate extremes, sovereign debt distress, geoeconomic fragmentation, and rapid AI-driven labor displacement. Traditional linear growth models—centered on fossil‑powered industrialization and export‑assembly manufacturing—are no longer viable. The document proposes a new development paradigm built on adaptive resilience, clean energy sovereignty, domestic industrial value capture, and digital public infrastructure. Across twelve analytical chapters, the monograph demonstrates—using empirical figures and cross‑regional data—that climate thermodynamics, infrastructure failure curves, battery storage cost deflation, mineral beneficiation multipliers, regenerative agritech, sponge metropolis engineering, and AI‑augmented vocational training collectively form a coherent strategic architecture for 21st‑century convergence. It shows, for example, that “upgrading design standards to climate‑resilient specifications… imposes a modest upfront capital expenditure premium of 8% to 12%” while preventing “35% to 54% of total asset value” in avoided losses (Chapter 2) . Likewise, domestic mineral refining multiplies national value capture by “5x to 14x per metric ton” compared to raw ore exports (Chapter 4) . The strategy centers on five sovereign pillars: Decentralized clean electrification to eliminate fossil‑import vulnerability and achieve 98%+ industrial power reliability. Green industrial upgrading through mandatory domestic refining of critical minerals and clean‑powered manufacturing clusters. Agrarian shock absorption using solar micro‑drip irrigation, biochar, inoculants, and AI agronomy to close 40–70% yield gaps. Resilient urban systems via sponge‑city infrastructure that reduces catastrophic flood losses by 65–75%. Digital public infrastructure (identity, payments, data exchange) to collapse transaction costs, expand financial inclusion, and eliminate fiscal leakages. The monograph concludes by quantifying a $3.2 trillion annual transition finance requirement for emerging economies and proposes a 2035 Polycrisis Compact that triples multilateral guarantee capacity to crowd in private capital at scale. This blended‑finance architecture—anchored in sovereign digital governance and mission‑oriented industrial policy—aims to convert polycrisis exposure into long‑term economic convergence for five billion people across the Global South.

title: Integrated Emergency Response Readiness Through Real-Time Field Intervention Team Drills: A Strategic Framework for Drill Design, Debriefing and The Measurement of Response Capability
source: Global Journal of Education Finance and Management
summary: Abstract : Employers across Southeast Asia are beginning to demand skills that match a greening economy, not only in environmental professions but across finance, manufacturing, construction, and services. Higher education systems in the re
content: Abstract : Employers across Southeast Asia are beginning to demand skills that match a greening economy, not only in environmental professions but across finance, manufacturing, construction, and services. Higher education systems in the region, however, differ sharply in how they equip graduates for this shift. This article compares green skills development policies in six ASEAN countries: Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, the Philippines, and Vietnam. Drawing on national policy documents, institutional strategies, and the scholarly literature, the comparison is organised around four dimensions: the depth of policy integration, the spread of sustainability content in curricula, investment in faculty development, and the strength of industry links for green skills. The findings show a wide gap between countries where green skills policy is coordinated at the system level (Singapore, Malaysia) and those where ambitious national targets have not yet produced widespread curriculum change (Vietnam, Philippines). Three bottlenecks cut across all six cases: the absence of discipline-specific green competency frameworks outside science and engineering, inadequate investment in training faculty to teach sustainability, and weak mechanisms for channelling green labour market intelligence into curriculum design. The article maps the current policy terrain and identifies leverage points for national reform, institutional strategy, and regional cooperation, including the potential of a regional qualifications framework for green competencies.

title: ШІ-ГРАМОТНІСТЬ ЯК ФАКТОР КОНКУРЕНТОСПРОМОЖНОСТІ ЛЮДСЬКОГО КАПІТАЛУ В ЦИФРОВІЙ МІЖНАРОДНІЙ ЕКОНОМІЦІ
source: Herald UNU International Economic Relations And World Economy
summary: У статті досліджено ШІ-грамотність як нову складову людського капіталу та чинник його конкурентоспроможності в цифровій міжнародній економіці. Обґрунтовано відмінність між базовим користуванням інструментами штучного інтелекту, спеціалізова
content: У статті досліджено ШІ-грамотність як нову складову людського капіталу та чинник його конкурентоспроможності в цифровій міжнародній економіці. Обґрунтовано відмінність між базовим користуванням інструментами штучного інтелекту, спеціалізованими ШІ-навичками та ШІ-грамотністю. Систематизовано канали впливу ШІ на трансформацію попиту на компетентності, продуктивність, зайнятість і міжнародну мобільність працівників. Запропоновано п’ятикомпонентну модель ШІ-грамотності, що охоплює концептуально-технологічну, прикладну, критично-верифікаційну, етико-регуляторну та адаптивно-комплементарну складові. Визначено напрями інтеграції цих компетентностей у підготовку фахівців з міжнародної економіки та окреслено підходи до подальшого вимірювання їх впливу на конкурентоспроможність людського капіталу.

title: INTERACTIVE DATA VISUALIZATION FOR FINANCIAL LITERACY EDUCATION: TECHNICAL PRINCIPLES, LEARNING APPLICATIONS, CHALLENGES, AND FUTURE DIRECTIONS
summary: Financial literacy requires learners to reason about quantities that change across time, interact under constraints, and remain uncertain. Compound growth, debt amortization, cash-flow trade-offs, diversification, and retirement adequacy ar
content: Financial literacy requires learners to reason about quantities that change across time, interact under constraints, and remain uncertain. Compound growth, debt amortization, cash-flow trade-offs, diversification, and retirement adequacy are therefore difficult to teach through definitions and isolated calculations alone. Interactive data visualization can make these relationships inspectable by connecting financial models with visual encoding, parameter manipulation, comparison, explanation, and feedback. This paper reviews the technical and instructional principles of interactive visualization for financial literacy education, including financial-model validity, graphical perception, interaction design, visualization literacy, cognitive load, uncertainty communication, and data storytelling. Applications include compound interest, budgeting and debt, risk–return and diversification, retirement planning, and learner-facing dashboards. The review argues that visual polish and interface activity are not learning mechanisms by themselves. Educational value depends on alignment among the target decision, model assumptions, representation, guided action, feedback, and transfer assessment. Major challenges include distortion, hidden assumptions, false precision, cognitive overload, uneven numeracy and graph literacy, accessibility barriers, privacy risks, commercial steering, and the substitution of clicks for evidence of learning. A model-aligned synthesis framework is outlined to connect financial questions, validated models, visual encoding, learner actions, diagnostic feedback, and independent assessment. Future systems should prioritize uncertainty-aware scenarios, transparent adaptation, multimodal accessibility, longitudinal evaluation, and reproducible benchmarks. Interactive visualization is most defensible as a structured environment for inquiry and explanation, not as a graphical shortcut to financial competence.

title: From openness to orchestration: the relationship between digital green orchestration capability and business model adaptation in complex environments
summary: This study examines the relationships of open innovation (OI) with the development of Digital Green Orchestration Capability (DGOC) and the integration of digital transformation and sustainability among manufacturing small and medium-sized
content: This study examines the relationships of open innovation (OI) with the development of Digital Green Orchestration Capability (DGOC) and the integration of digital transformation and sustainability among manufacturing small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). It further examines the effects of DGOC on business model adaptation and firm performance under conditions of environmental complexity. A quantitative survey was conducted among 232 Iranian manufacturing SMEs. The proposed research model was tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4.0, incorporating mediation, moderation, and nonlinear analyses. The results show that inbound OI positively influences DGOC, whereas outbound OI exhibits an inverted U-shaped relationship, indicating that excessive openness reduces orchestration effectiveness. DGOC is positively associated with business model adaptation and statistically mediates the relationship between OI and organizational adaptation. Environmental complexity strengthens the effects of DGOC on both business model adaptation and firm performance. However, the direct association between business model adaptation and firm performance was positive but not statistically significant in this cross-sectional sample. This result indicates that a clear performance association was not observed at the time of data collection; future longitudinal research should examine whether such benefits materialize over time. This study introduces and empirically validates DGOC as a novel dynamic capability that integrates digital transformation, sustainability, and ecosystem collaboration within a unified orchestration framework. By combining dynamic capabilities theory, open innovation, and complexity theory, it advances understanding of how SMEs convert external knowledge into coordinated digital and green transformation in complex environments while providing practical guidance for managers and policymakers seeking to enhance organizational adaptability.

title: Financial Law for Silver Economy Development
source: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)
summary: Population aging is increasing the need for financial frameworks capable of supporting the development of the silver economy. This article examines the principal components of financial law relevant to mobilizing, using, and allocating fina
content: Population aging is increasing the need for financial frameworks capable of supporting the development of the silver economy. This article examines the principal components of financial law relevant to mobilizing, using, and allocating financial resources for silver-economy development. Drawing on legal analysis and selected international experiences, it considers the roles of State-budget resources, private investment, credit, taxation, and other financial mechanisms. The analysis shows that an appropriate combination of public and private resources can support essential services for older persons while encouraging investment and innovation. The article proposes recommendations for countries experiencing population aging to strengthen financial laws governing resource mobilization, resource use, and the allocation of funds generated through silver-economy activities.

title: Supply Chain Flexibility in Modern Markets: The Impact of Technological Integration, Workforce Agility, and Supplier Relationship Management through Operational Responsiveness
source: WSEAS TRANSACTIONS ON BUSINESS AND ECONOMICS
summary: Supply chain flexibility is vital for firms operating in dynamic, technology-driven environments. This study examines how technology integration, workforce agility, supplier relationship management, and operational responsiveness influence
content: Supply chain flexibility is vital for firms operating in dynamic, technology-driven environments. This study examines how technology integration, workforce agility, supplier relationship management, and operational responsiveness influence flexible supply chains. Grounded in dynamic capabilities theory and adaptive supply chain management, the study develops a framework linking organizational strategy to supply chain agility. Data were collected through a survey of 244 professionals from manufacturing and distribution firms in Bangladesh and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling. Results show that technology integration and supplier relationship management significantly enhance supply chain flexibility, while workforce agility is the strongest predictor of operational responsiveness. However, operational responsiveness does not significantly mediate the relationships between the explanatory variables and supply chain flexibility. The findings suggest that flexibility depends more on strategic managerial capabilities than responsiveness alone. This study contributes by integrating technological, human, and relational capabilities within a predictive model for emerging-market supply chains.

title: Reposisi Tanggung Jawab Komisaris atas Tindakan Ultra Vires yang Menimbulkan Pelanggaran CSR
source: CARONG Jurnal Pendidikan Sosial dan Humaniora
summary: The principle of limited liability in a corporation serves as the basis for limiting the liability of corporate organs, namely the General Meeting of Shareholders (GMS), Board of Directors, and Board of Commissioners, for losses incurred by
content: The principle of limited liability in a corporation serves as the basis for limiting the liability of corporate organs, namely the General Meeting of Shareholders (GMS), Board of Directors, and Board of Commissioners, for losses incurred by the corporation. However, ultra vires acts committed or tolerated by the Board of Commissioners may result in violations of Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) obligations, causing social and environmental harm. This study aims to analyze and reposition the legal liability of the Board of Commissioners for ultra vires acts that result in CSR violations within the framework of corporate law reform. This study employs a normative juridical method using conceptual and comparative approaches and examines the interrelationship among the doctrines of fiduciary duty, ultra vires, piercing the corporate veil, and the development of the concept of personal liability of commissioners. The findings indicate that positive law continues to treat CSR primarily as a corporate obligation, thereby creating an accountability gap when violations arise from acts of commissioners that exceed their authority. Repositioning the liability of commissioners is therefore necessary through a broader interpretation of fiduciary duty and the selective application of the piercing the corporate veil doctrine. Such an approach is expected to strengthen commissioner accountability, prevent ultra vires acts, and promote the protection of public interests in the implementation of CSR.

title: Implementation Readiness Across Heterogeneous Local Climate Plans: A Longitudinal Documentary Assessment of Gaziantep, Türkiye
summary: Municipal climate plans differ in policy purpose and documentary coverage, complicating comparisons of their preparedness for implementation. This study examines how plan-based implementation readiness varies across four climate-planning ep
content: Municipal climate plans differ in policy purpose and documentary coverage, complicating comparisons of their preparedness for implementation. This study examines how plan-based implementation readiness varies across four climate-planning episodes in Gaziantep, Türkiye, between 2016 and 2023. A two-axis framework distinguishes policy purpose, diagnostic foundations, and target architecture from 18 common delivery functions; it assesses documentary specification rather than institutional capacity or implementation performance. Criterion-level document analysis is supported by sensitivity analyses addressing unequal observability and evidence form. The 2016 Climate Change Action Plan already specified prioritisation, sequencing, responsibility, costing, and emissions monitoring. The 2023 Green City Action Plan systematically specified all assessed delivery functions, while the Climate Change Adaptation Action Plan combined explicit feasibility and participatory provisions with arrangements for monitoring and adaptive review. Nevertheless, later plans were not uniformly stronger: some functions remained stable, others were less systematically specified, and delivery arrangements took different forms. This interpretation remained consistent across sensitivity scenarios, although several adaptation-plan findings depended on executive-summary evidence.
