Conversely, in Sweden, operational scale and efficiency signals are largely neutral in annual sector and pooled regressions (with scale predictability confined to monthly Chemicals returns), whereas carbon costs (EUA) strongly penalize Chemicals at the annual horizon and forward electricity prices ( Fwd ) emerge only in the physical pooled panel and excess-return specifications. A complementary firm-level case study of 144 Italian foundries illustrates the sensitivity of the micro-to-macro transmission channel: while real returns show positive but statistically imprecise scale effects, excess-return specifications reveal strong short-term mean reversion in firm scale alongside dominant carbon-pricing risk. Overall, our findings indicate that energy scale and efficiency innovations contain distinct predictive content at annual horizons, but their pricing is regime- and specification-dependent, a pattern consistent with differences in the institutional and operational structure of national electricity markets.

title: Provincial Carbon Inequality and the Effectiveness of Green Finance Development in China
summary: ABSTRACT Development disparities within regions cause carbon inequality (CI), which exacerbates the Chinese unbalanced development problem. However, there is still a lack of research that measures CI from the aspect of intra‐regional differ
content: ABSTRACT Development disparities within regions cause carbon inequality (CI), which exacerbates the Chinese unbalanced development problem. However, there is still a lack of research that measures CI from the aspect of intra‐regional differences and examines its impact factors. Using sub‐provincial data covering 420 cities, counties, and districts, this study measures CI in 30 Chinese provinces and investigates the influence of green finance (GF) on CI and the role of climate risk (CR) in the GF‐CI linkage. Several findings have been found. First, using the population‐weighted Williamson index to capture intra‐provincial disparities, our analysis reveals pronounced regional variation in CI, with the East and Middle regions following a U‐shaped pattern between 2008 and 2017, while the West experiences a consistent decline. Second, the dynamic panel analysis reveals that GF can reduce CI, particularly in midwestern regions and provinces characterised by lower carbon intensity. Third, the moderating effect demonstrates that climate risk (CR) weakens the inhibitory role of GF on CI. Under low CR, GF mitigates CI, whereas when CR exceeds a critical threshold, the beneficial effect of GF is reversed. This study contributes empirical insights for policymakers seeking to mitigate CI through financial instruments.

title: Photo‐Enhanced Electronic Metal–Support Interaction Boosts Low‐Temperature Water–Gas Shift Reaction via Ni δ+ –O V –Ce 3+ Interfacial Redox Cycling
summary: ABSTRACT Nickel (Ni) is an attractive non‐noble‐metal catalyst for the water‐gas shift reaction (WGSR), yet strong CO adsorption and competing methanation severely limit its activity and selectivity. Herein, we develop a series of NiCe laye
content: ABSTRACT Nickel (Ni) is an attractive non‐noble‐metal catalyst for the water‐gas shift reaction (WGSR), yet strong CO adsorption and competing methanation severely limit its activity and selectivity. Herein, we develop a series of NiCe layered double hydroxide‐derived catalysts (NCO‐ T ) through reduction‐induced Ni exsolution. The optimized NCO‐450 catalyst achieves 92.53% CO conversion and an H 2 production rate of 103.24 µmol·g cat −1 ·s −1 at ambient pressure and a catalyst temperature of 83°C. In situ spectroscopic analyses and theoretical calculations reveal that isolated interfacial oxygen vacancies (O V s) stabilize the active Ni δ+ ─O V ─Ce 3+ motif responsible for the superior WGSR performance. Photoexcitation‐induced directional interfacial charge transfer from Ni to CeO 2‐ x enhances the electronic metal–support interaction and continuously regenerates this active interfacial state, thereby moderating CO adsorption, promoting H 2 O activation, and suppressing competing methanation. This work offers a rational design strategy for developing low‐cost transition‐metal catalysts with superior low‐temperature activity and high selectivity.

title: Does Digital Transformation Drive the Adjustment of Bank Loan Structure? Evidence From China
summary: ABSTRACT This article examines the impact of digital transformation on bank loan structure. We employ text mining and the entropy weight method to measure the five‐dimensional digital transformation index of banks and conduct an empirical a
content: ABSTRACT This article examines the impact of digital transformation on bank loan structure. We employ text mining and the entropy weight method to measure the five‐dimensional digital transformation index of banks and conduct an empirical analysis based on the panel data of 132 commercial banks in China from 2013 to 2022. The results indicate that digital transformation significantly drives the adjustment of various types of bank loan structures, increasing the proportion of unsecured loans, personal loans, medium‐ and long‐term loans, manufacturing loans, and green loans. In terms of the impact mechanism, improving information screening capability and enhancing risk control capability are two key channels through which digital transformation exerts its impact. Furthermore, the heterogeneity analysis reveals that the impact of digital transformation on loan structures varies among banks with different asset size, profitability, and management efficiency. Finally, we propose targeted suggestions for commercial banks and regulatory authorities.

title: Green retrofitting in ceramics manufacturing industry: a hybrid LLM-MCDM approach
summary: This study examines strategic retrofitting in high-end artistic ceramics manufacturing under stringent “Dual Carbon” regulations. Balancing regulatory compliance with artisanal integrity represents a significant industrial challenge. To add
content: This study examines strategic retrofitting in high-end artistic ceramics manufacturing under stringent “Dual Carbon” regulations. Balancing regulatory compliance with artisanal integrity represents a significant industrial challenge. To address this multidimensional problem, this research develops an integrated hybrid multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) framework combining the Full Consistency Method (FUCOM) and the Measurement of Alternatives and Ranking according to Compromise Solution (MARCOS). Gemini 1.5 Pro was employed exclusively as a “Synthetic Knowledge Engineer” to extract and organise candidate criteria from five authoritative regulatory and technical documents, which were subsequently validated and refined by a multidisciplinary human expert panel to construct the Evaluation Index System (EIS). FUCOM results indicate that “Environmental Compliance and Process Monitoring” is the most influential main criterion, while “Specific Energy Intensity”, “Weighted Flue Gas Emissions” and “Payback Period and ROI” emerge as the most important sub-criteria. The MARCOS evaluation identifies the “Hybrid Evolutionary Path” as the highest-ranked compromise pathway, reflecting a phased investment strategy that balances emission reduction objectives with capital constraints. Sensitivity analyses and comparative assessments using established MCDM methods, including TOPSIS, COPRAS, WASPAS and VIKOR, demonstrate a high degree of ranking stability under the tested analytical conditions. The proposed framework provides a transparent and potentially transferable decision-support approach to facilitate low-carbon transitions in traditional craft-based manufacturing industries.

title: Residential Energy Consumption Patterns and Efficiency Awareness: A Case Study of Ajelat City
source: AlQalam Journal of Medical and Applied Sciences
summary: Conserving electricity in homes is a crucial aspect of addressing the challenges of climate change, meeting the need for greater energy efficiency, and avoiding total blackouts caused by excessive electricity consumption. This study aims to
content: Conserving electricity in homes is a crucial aspect of addressing the challenges of climate change, meeting the need for greater energy efficiency, and avoiding total blackouts caused by excessive electricity consumption. This study aims to evaluate energy conservation and efficiency awareness practices of households in Ajelat City, Libya. The study also examined the level of energy conservation practices and the extent of their variation, as well as the level of awareness and education regarding energy saving among households. Also, the analysis of household characteristics which participate in this study. Data were collected using Google Form through a questionnaire consisting of 16 items. The total number of respondents was 88 male and female households. The data were analyzed by using SPSS program software. Quantitative data were analysed using frequency and percentage (demographic variables). The findings show that most respondents were male and married, and had a higher level of education. The majority of them were government employees. The results also showed that the level of awareness regarding energy conservation among households is low; while some families were able to explain the concept, the vast majority were unfamiliar with it. This is attributed not only to the inadequacy of energy conservation awareness campaigns in the region but also to the methods used to effectively convey this information to households—whether through local outreach or the General Electricity Company.

title: Functional refurbishment of Villino Abetti, improvement of energy efficiency and carbon neutrality at Arcetri Observatory
Consumers with high shares of organic food consumption are more likely to feel obliged to reduce the climate impact of their food – a segment-level analysis based on two separate datasets
summary: Abstract This study investigated the extent to which consumers with high organic consumption are more climate-oriented than segments of consumers with low organic consumption. We did this by identifying comparable organic Light user and Sup
content: Abstract This study investigated the extent to which consumers with high organic consumption are more climate-oriented than segments of consumers with low organic consumption. We did this by identifying comparable organic Light user and Super user segments in two separate datasets and comparing attitudinal and behavioural patterns across segments. We found that the Super users felt a stronger obligation to reduce their climate impact than Light users based on responses to an online survey. Moreover, we identified four barriers to transitioning towards a more climate-friendly diet. Both of the segments of consumers that we study faced barriers in terms of low priority for climate-friendly food when shopping and perceived practical barriers in terms of not knowing what to buy, where to find it, or how to prepare it. Additionally, Light users more often faced barriers in terms of negative attitudes towards climate-friendly food, and they perceived climate-friendly food to be too expensive. The other dataset consisting of observed household purchase data revealed that the households with the highest organic budget shares allocated lower shares of their total food budgets to beef and pork and higher shares to vegetables than Light user households. This could indicate a more climate-friendly purchase pattern among Super users than Light users. The differences between the Light user and Super user segments found in the two datasets indicate that different motivational tools may be needed to encourage the two segments to shift towards more climate-friendly eating habits.

title: High-surface-area activated carbon from menengiç (Pistacia terebinthus) fruit shells for efficient removal of carbofuran from water
summary: Abstract The widespread use of pesticides poses significant risks to aquatic environments and human health, necessitating effective removal strategies. In this study, activated carbon was produced from menengiç ( Pistacia terebinthus ) frui
content: Abstract The widespread use of pesticides poses significant risks to aquatic environments and human health, necessitating effective removal strategies. In this study, activated carbon was produced from menengiç ( Pistacia terebinthus ) fruit shells and evaluated for carbofuran removal from aqueous solutions. KOH activation yielded a predominantly microporous structure with a BET surface area of 2167 m² g⁻¹, as confirmed by nitrogen adsorption–desorption analysis, SEM, and XPS. The adsorbent exhibited rapid adsorption, reaching equilibrium within 25 min, with optimal performance at pH 3 and an adsorbent dosage of 5 mg. The maximum adsorption capacity reached 307.3 mg g⁻¹ at 298 K and decreased as the temperature increased. Adsorption equilibrium data were best described by the Langmuir model, indicating predominantly monolayer adsorption under the conditions investigated. Thermodynamic parameters indicated that the adsorption process was spontaneous and exothermic. Regeneration experiments demonstrated that approximately 91.6% of the initial adsorption capacity was retained after five adsorption–desorption cycles. In addition, the adsorbent maintained approximately 88% of its original adsorption capacity in a simulated wastewater matrix containing competing ions and natural organic matter. The results indicate that menengiç fruit shell–derived activated carbon is a promising adsorbent for carbofuran removal from water and merits further investigation for practical water treatment applications.

title: Evaluation of free lime content in cement kilns by physics-guided support vector regression using factory energy management system
summary: The cement industry is one of the most carbon-intensive industrial sectors owing to its high energy demand. In clinker production, free lime (F-CaO) is a critical quality indicator that reflects the adequacy of heat supply during high-tempe
content: The cement industry is one of the most carbon-intensive industrial sectors owing to its high energy demand. In clinker production, free lime (F-CaO) is a critical quality indicator that reflects the adequacy of heat supply during high-temperature processing; excessive F-CaO indicates insufficient thermal energy and leads to deterioration of clinker quality and energy efficiency. Accurate prediction of F-CaO is therefore important for effective quality control and energy-efficient plant operation. Previous data-driven studies have selected input variables mainly from statistical correlations, often neglecting the underlying heat-transfer and reaction mechanisms of the pyro-process. To address this limitation, the energy flows and airflow distribution in the pre-heater, kiln, and cooler were quantified using a factory energy management system (FEMS) combined with a heat and mass balance model. Based on this analysis, physically meaningful input variables governing F-CaO formation were derived and incorporated into a support vector regression (SVR) model. Under an identical chronological train/test split and hyperparameter optimization protocol, the physics-guided inputs showed improved prediction performance compared with conventional correlation-based inputs, achieving MSE = 0.03, TIC = 0.07, and R = 0.73 on the hold-out test set. These results indicate that deriving input variables from physical principles can improve F-CaO prediction consistency within the studied operating window, providing a rational framework for physics-guided soft sensor development.

title: Does Greenwashing Perception Influence the Job‐Seeking Intention of Business Students? The Role of Perceived Green Corporate Image and Recruitment Buzz
source: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
summary: ABSTRACT Drawing on the Affect‐Behavior‐Cognition (ABC) model, this study examines how greenwashing perception shapes the job‐seeking intentions of final‐year business students in Ghana. Specifically, the study theorizes and tests the moder
content: ABSTRACT Drawing on the Affect‐Behavior‐Cognition (ABC) model, this study examines how greenwashing perception shapes the job‐seeking intentions of final‐year business students in Ghana. Specifically, the study theorizes and tests the moderating role of perceived green corporate image and recruitment buzz. Data from 179 final‐year business students at the University of Ghana Business School were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS‐SEM). The findings reveal that green‐washing perception positively and significantly influences the intention to apply for jobs. Importantly, perceived green corporate image amplifies this effect, indicating that a strong green reputation heightens applicants' sensitivity to greenwashing signals. Conversely, recruitment buzz attenuates the relationship, suggesting that compelling recruitment communications can offset greenwashing skepticism. The study contributes to the nascent literature on green employer branding and recruitment by offering rare evidence from a Sub‐Saharan African context, and carries actionable implications for HR practitioners, corporate communications professionals, and policymakers in developing economies.

title: Efficient Thermo‐Photocatalytic Methanation of Dilute CO 2 via N‐Doped Carbon Encapsulated Co/CoO Nanoparticles
summary: ABSTRACT Thermo‐photocatalytic CO 2 methanation represents an attractive strategy for addressing global energy and environmental challenges. However, achieving efficient low‐temperature methanation using low‐concentration CO 2 feedstocks re
content: ABSTRACT Thermo‐photocatalytic CO 2 methanation represents an attractive strategy for addressing global energy and environmental challenges. However, achieving efficient low‐temperature methanation using low‐concentration CO 2 feedstocks remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report a nitrogen‐doped carbon (NC)‐encapsulated cobalt nanoparticle catalyst decorated with CoO particles for low‐temperature dilute CO 2 methanation under LED irradiation. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that pyridinic‐N in the NC matrix enhances CO 2 adsorption, enabling the catalyst to react with 0.04% low‐concentration CO 2 . Metallic Co nanoparticles function as active sites for H 2 dissociation, whereas CoO promotes the generation of photogenerated electrons to facilitate CO 2 activation. Under light irradiation, H 2 dissociates into active hydrogen species, which subsequently undergo thermally assisted spillover to CO 2 adsorption sites to form the critical COOH* intermediate. The synergistic effect between photoirradiation and thermal input effectively reduces the operating temperature required for catalytic methanation. Accordingly, the optimal catalyst achieves exceptional performance at 180°C under 420 nm light irradiation, delivering a CH 4 production rate of 344.76 μmol g −1 h −1 , with nearly 100% CH 4 selectivity and 91.6% CO 2 conversion. This work provides a new perspective for the design of high‐performance catalysts for efficient low‐concentration CO 2 conversion.

title: Rooftop solar supports carbon-neutral transition in Hong Kong’s building sector
summary: Rooftop solar systems are pivotal for carbon neutrality and urban sustainability, yet accurate assessment of rooftop solar energy potential remains constrained by coarse representation of complex building forms, incomplete characterization
content: Rooftop solar systems are pivotal for carbon neutrality and urban sustainability, yet accurate assessment of rooftop solar energy potential remains constrained by coarse representation of complex building forms, incomplete characterization of cloud variability, and limited integration of technical, economic, and policy factors. Here we show that a machine learning framework integrating high-frequency satellite and ground observations can estimate rooftop solar energy potential at 0.5-meter resolution for 338,550 buildings in Hong Kong. Despite substantial reductions associated with cloud cover and temperature, total citywide potential reaches 3.77 terawatt-hours per year. This resource could avoid 24.9 billion kilograms of carbon dioxide emissions over its lifetime and enable 18.9% of commercial buildings with energy storage to achieve local decarbonization targets. Supported by local feed-in tariffs, average financial payback periods range from 3.49 to 6.42 years, with more than 90% of buildings meeting household affordability thresholds. These findings provide actionable guidance for solar deployment, investment decisions, and urban energy planning in dense, cloud-prone cities worldwide. Hong Kong rooftops could generate 3.77 terawatt-hours of solar electricity annually, avoid 24.9 billion kilograms of carbon dioxide, and deliver payback within 3.49–6.42 years, according to a machine learning framework integrating high-frequency satellite and ground observations.’

title: Ophiopogonin D suppresses non-small cell lung cancer progression by targeting exosomal MALAT1 to enhance dendritic cell maturation
summary: Tumor-immune cell crosstalk critically shapes the progression of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet the mechanisms underlying exosome-mediated immune suppression remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify a previously unrecogniz
content: Tumor-immune cell crosstalk critically shapes the progression of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet the mechanisms underlying exosome-mediated immune suppression remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify a previously unrecognized exosomal lncRNA-mediated immunoregulatory axis targeted by the natural compound Ophiopogonin D (OP-D). Transcriptomic profiling and mechanistic rescue experiments revealed that Lewis lung carcinoma (LLC)-derived exosomal MALAT1 suppresses dendritic cell (DC) maturation by increasing SIRT1 expression and attenuating p65 phosphorylation. Computational modeling combined with molecular dynamics simulation predicted a stable interaction between OP-D and MALAT1, which was further validated by biolayer interferometry (BLI) and microscale thermophoresis (MST) assays, supporting MALAT1 as a direct molecular target of OP-D. In vivo, OP-D markedly inhibited tumor growth and enhanced intratumoral DC activation. Mechanistically, OP-D reduced MALAT1 abundance in LLC-derived exosomes and decreased the accumulation of exosomal MALAT1 in recipient DCs, thereby suppressing SIRT1 signaling, restoring p65 phosphorylation, and promoting DC maturation and antitumor immune responses. Furthermore, MALAT1 overexpression attenuated the immunostimulatory effects of OP-D, confirming the functional importance of the exosomal MALAT1-SIRT1/p-p65 axis. Collectively, these findings identify exosomal MALAT1 as a critical mediator of tumor-induced DC dysfunction and establish OP-D as a promising immunomodulatory natural compound capable of reprogramming tumor-immune communication in NSCLC.

title: Humans as predators of the biosphere: Consumer-resource techno-dynamics and its implications for sustainability
summary: Modern human societies and their socioeconomies impose immense consumption demands on the biosphere, departing from common ecological rules. This detachment makes it urgent to understand the implications of human population growth and consu
content: Modern human societies and their socioeconomies impose immense consumption demands on the biosphere, departing from common ecological rules. This detachment makes it urgent to understand the implications of human population growth and consumption dynamics for sustainable trajectories. Models coupling human growth, technology and the biosphere either omit the biosphere as a dynamical variable, restrict technological effects to a single component of the coupled system, or become too complex for analytic stability analysis. Missing is a simple framework in which technology independently modulates population support and per capita biosphere consumption while retaining analytic tractability and allowing confrontation with long-run global data. We address this gap with an ecological consumer–resource model of the human–biosphere system. We separate technological effects into parameters for population support per unit organic carbon and for per capita consumption. Their combination defines a single compound technological impact. We then compare three functional relations: predator–prey, population-driven and supply–demand. For each, we derive the parameter space of stable coexistence. Finally, we calibrate the model to more than 150 years of reconstructed global data to identify technological regimes and locate the present-day system within the stability landscape. Two of the three relations admit Hopf bifurcations and regions without coexistence, while only supply–demand consumption opens a basin toward finite-time biosphere depletion. An extended model combining the three relations provides the best fit to the data and reveals a shift from predator–prey toward supply–demand consumption in recent decades. The supply–demand mechanism dominates the most recent segment in 82% of bootstrap replicates. This attribution remains unchanged under ± 20 % perturbations of the fixed parameters. With the recent regime held fixed, the present-day state follows a biosphere-depleting trajectory in 88% of bootstrap replicates. The immediate threat is therefore not Hopf instability under predator–prey dynamics, but a supply–demand regime in which finite-time biosphere depletion becomes dynamically accessible. The model warns that demographic transition alone is not enough for sustainable trajectories. Consumption efficiency and the form of consumption dynamics are also important for reducing the compound technological impact and shifting the system toward sustainable dynamics.

title: Review of Pilot-Scale Carbon-Negative Pulping Technologies Using Agricultural Residues: Technical, Economic, and LCA Perspectives
source: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)
summary: This review synthesizes findings from 28 pilot-scale studies on pulping agricultural residues, including bagasse, wheat straw, and rice straw, integrated with bioenergy recovery and carbon capture and storage (CCS). The reviewed studies ind
content: This review synthesizes findings from 28 pilot-scale studies on pulping agricultural residues, including bagasse, wheat straw, and rice straw, integrated with bioenergy recovery and carbon capture and storage (CCS). The reviewed studies indicate pulp yields typically ranging from 40-48%, carbon capture efficiencies around 85%, and the potential for low or negative greenhouse-gas emissions under favorable economic conditions. The pulp and paper industry faces increasing pressure to reduce greenhouse gas emissions while maintaining reliable fiber supply and product quality. Agricultural residues represent a promising alternative to conventional wood feedstocks and can contribute to diversification of fiber resources. When integrated with bioenergy recovery and carbon capture technologies, these systems may significantly reduce the carbon footprint of pulp production. Many previous investigations have relied primarily on laboratory experiments or modeling approaches, with limited integrated pilot-scale evidence addressing technical performance, economic feasibility, and life-cycle environmental impacts. This review compiles and analyzes pilot-scale data on pulping performance, energy balance, carbon capture efficiency, techno-economic indicators (CAPEX $2.5-4.0 million per ktpy; OPEX $620-750 per tonne of pulp), and life-cycle assessment results. The synthesis indicates that agricultural-residue pulping can achieve pulp quality comparable to conventional processes while offering significant opportunities for emission reduction when combined with bioenergy and CCS integration. Economic competitiveness depends strongly on residue availability, energy integration efficiency, and carbon pricing mechanisms ($30-100 per t CO?). Life-cycle assessments further identify transportation logistics and process energy consumption as major contributors to overall environmental impacts. Overall, the reviewed literature indicates that carbon-negative pulping based on agricultural residues is technically feasible at pilot scale and may become economically viable under favorable policy and market conditions. This synthesis provides an integrated overview of current pilot-scale evidence and highlights the potential role of agricultural residues and carbon capture technologies in advancing sustainable pulp production.

title: Green Marketing Strategies Adopted by Ecopreneurs for Environmental Protection and Sustainable Development: A Study with Special Reference to Selected Indian Companies
summary: Introduction: Green marketing is a vital business strategy promoting environmentally friendly products and practices, significantly influenced by rising global awareness of ecological issues. Originating in the 1980s, it emphasizes sustaina
content: Introduction: Green marketing is a vital business strategy promoting environmentally friendly products and practices, significantly influenced by rising global awareness of ecological issues. Originating in the 1980s, it emphasizes sustainability across product development, packaging, and supply chains, reflecting a brand's commitment to social responsibility. As public awareness of global warming and pollution increases, demand for eco-friendly products continues to rise across various sectors, including consumer goods, industrial products, and services. Methodology: The paper utilizes secondary data sourced from a variety of research papers, journals, articles, reports, and relevant company websites, ensuring a comprehensive analysis of existing literature and information for its conclusions. It is organised around two objectives: to study the concept of green marketing and its challenges, and to explain the green marketing strategies adopted by some selected Indian ecopreneurs for environmental protection and sustainable development. The literature reviewed covers Sathish T (2024) on green marketing in the digital era, Soumen Nath, Soumi Chakraborty and Kallal Banerjee (2023) on green marketing and sustainable development in India, Geetesh Yadav (2022) on the three R's, Sunita P. Kharate (2021) on the Indian context, Szabo and Webster (2020) on perceived greenwashing, Mukonza and Swarts (2019) on retail sector performance, and Amoako et al. (2018) on green marketing and the SDGs. Results & Discussion: Green marketing strategies are documented across four company categories. Among FMCG companies, Colgate-Palmolive targets net-zero carbon emissions by 2040, 100% recyclable packaging by 2025 and sustainable sourcing; Hindustan Unilever prioritises reducing plastic usage, sustainable sourcing, biodegradable ingredients and recycled plastics; and Dabur India has eliminated carton packaging for Dabur Red Toothpaste under its Project Prakriti strategy, aiming for net-zero emissions by 2045 and water positivity by 2030. Among e-retailers, Amazon has eliminated single-use plastics in its Indian fulfilment centres since December 2019 and targets a 50% reduction in shipment emissions by 2030, while Myntra runs Myntra Circular and the Myntra for Earth store. Among MNCs, Infosys and TCS pursue green IT, green buildings and sustainable supply chains, and Wipro's Green ware range is RoHS compliant. Among conglomerates, ITC invests in renewable energy and water stewardship, Reliance Industries targets net-zero carbon by 2035, and L&T targets carbon neutrality by 2040 and water neutrality by 2035. Conclusion: The study highlights the interconnectedness of green marketing and sustainable development in India, pointing to globalization as a catalyst for businesses to embrace eco-friendly practices in response to rising consumer environmental awareness. It indicates that these initiatives can enhance economic, social, and environmental progress in the country. Ho

title: Managing the Green Economy through Digital Technologies: Opportunities, Mechanisms, and Prospects
source: Journal of Economic Development Innovation and Policy
summary: This article analyzes the theoretical and methodological foundations, practical mechanisms, and prospects of managing the green economy through digital technologies. The interrelationship between the green economy and digital transformation
content: This article analyzes the theoretical and methodological foundations, practical mechanisms, and prospects of managing the green economy through digital technologies. The interrelationship between the green economy and digital transformation is examined from the perspective of the "twin transition." The study substantiates the role of artificial intelligence, Big Data, the Internet of Things (IoT), and blockchain technologies in improving energy efficiency, tracking carbon footprints, managing waste, and shaping green finance flows, and proposes institutional mechanisms for their governance. Drawing on a comparative analysis of international experience (the European Union, China, the United Arab Emirates, the United Kingdom, and Singapore) and Uzbekistan's practice, supported by official statistical data, the authors develop an original conceptual model, the "digital-green governance cycle," together with practical recommendations for managing the digital-green transition in Uzbekistan. The research methodology combines systems analysis, a comparative-historical approach, and the generalization of statistical data.

title: CARBON EMISSION ANALYSIS OF PT TOBA BARA SEJAHTERA (TBS) ENERGI UTAMA TBK BASED ON SUSTAINABILITY REPORT
source: Count Journal of Accounting Business and Management
summary: This study analyzes carbon emissions of PT Toba Bara Sejahtera (TBS) Energi Utama Tbk during 2020-2022 as a case study of an energy company transitioning from fossil fuels to renewable energy. Using a descriptive qualitative approach with s
content: This study analyzes carbon emissions of PT Toba Bara Sejahtera (TBS) Energi Utama Tbk during 2020-2022 as a case study of an energy company transitioning from fossil fuels to renewable energy. Using a descriptive qualitative approach with secondary data from sustainability reports, the research reveals a surge in GHG emissions from 230,135 tCO₂eq (2020) to 1,373,012.34 tCO₂eq (2022), a nearly six-fold increase driven by full operation of two 200 MW coal-fired power plants. Emission intensity rose from 1,125.8 to 1,920.8 tCO₂eq per million USD revenue. TBS's reporting practices align with GHG Protocol standards for Scope 1 and 2, but require improved methodological transparency and comprehensive Scope 3 disclosure. The study uncovers an energy transition paradox where long-term decarbonization commitments face short-term emission increases from existing fossil assets. The 2024 divestment of coal power plants is projected to reduce emissions by 85%, marking a transformative phase toward the 2030 carbon neutrality target. This research contributes to Indonesia's sustainability reporting literature and provides decarbonization strategy recommendations for transitioning energy companies.

title: A multi-level dataset of China’s energy-transition policies from national to prefecture levels over 2000–2024
summary: China’s energy transition has generated a vast and heterogeneous body of policy documents across multiple administrative levels. Existing datasets, however, remain largely confined to national-level analyses or single-domain applications an
content: China’s energy transition has generated a vast and heterogeneous body of policy documents across multiple administrative levels. Existing datasets, however, remain largely confined to national-level analyses or single-domain applications and rely predominantly on proxy variables or keyword-frequency methods that may inadequately capture the substantive content of policy texts. To address this gap, this study constructs a title-anchored, multi-level inventory of China’s energy-transition policies spanning 2000 to 2024, based on an exact-match search of seven selected energy-transition-related terms in official policy titles, yielding 7,295 policy texts retrieved from PKULaw across national, provincial, and prefecture-level administrative tiers. Each policy is annotated with 14 structured metadata fields and classified according to a four-category objective typology with 16 sub-objectives and a three-category instrument typology with 9 subcategories. Multi-label classification allows each policy to carry multiple objectives and instruments simultaneously. The dataset is designed to support empirical research on policy mix composition, multi-level governance, and the drivers of energy transition outcomes at regional and firm levels.

title: Thermodynamic perspective on human-building interaction entropy, comfort and energy flow
summary: This study presents a thermodynamic interpretation of how humans and buildings interact, focusing on entropy dynamics, comfort perception, and internal energy exchanges. Human thermal adaptation is treated as an open, non-equilibrium proces
content: This study presents a thermodynamic interpretation of how humans and buildings interact, focusing on entropy dynamics, comfort perception, and internal energy exchanges. Human thermal adaptation is treated as an open, non-equilibrium process in which energy and matter are continuously exchanged to sustain thermal stability. Physiological and behavioral adjustments are therefore described as entropy-modulating actions that influence both comfort and system performance. By considering the combined human–environment domain, the total entropy balance may become locally positive or negative while still adhering to the second law of thermodynamics at the universal scale. Entropy generation is employed as a diagnostic variable for assessing human thermal stress, comfort response, and overall energy quality within indoor environments. The resulting framework integrates human adaptation and building physics, enabling a coherent evaluation of comfort, efficiency, and sustainability in low-exergy design.

title: Can Class 3 e-bikes help meet California's VMT and climate goals? A mobility-substitution screening
summary: Abstract Transportation is California’s largest source of greenhouse gas emissions, and vehicle electrification alone does not reduce vehicle-miles traveled (VMT). This paper asks whether Class 3 e-bikes—pedal-assisted to 28 mph—could repla
content: Abstract Transportation is California’s largest source of greenhouse gas emissions, and vehicle electrification alone does not reduce vehicle-miles traveled (VMT). This paper asks whether Class 3 e-bikes—pedal-assisted to 28 mph—could replace some of the intermediate-distance commutes that conventional bicycles rarely serve. Using 2024 LOCUS mobility data for Los Angeles County, we define an addressable commute band (ACB) as weekday peak-period Motorized travel of 5–15 miles one way. This market contains 11.98 million passenger-miles per weekday, while conventional bicycles account for only about 0.3% of passenger-miles under the same filters. European speed-pedelec evidence shows that these distances are within routine operating range. Because LOCUS includes e-bikes within Motorized travel, the scenarios explicitly vary both the automobile share of that category and the share of Class 3 travel that actually replaces car travel. In the upper-bound full-substitution case, a 10% shift removes 283 million vehicle-miles and 101.6 ktCO2e per year. That is 5.6 times LA Metro’s published bikeway VMT benefit, mainly because the trips considered here are longer. Yet the same scenario removes only about 0.43% of modeled county passenger VMT, and the 30% stress test about 1.3%. Class 3 e-bikes are therefore a potentially important intermediate-distance option, but only one part of the much larger mobility transition required in California.

title: Influence of stack voltage window, driving cycle, and HVAC strategy on hydrogen consumption in a fuel cell electric bus
summary: This study investigates the energy efficiency and operational behaviour of a hydrogen fuel cell electric bus (FCEB) under different fuel cell stack voltage windows, driving cycles, and heating, ventilation and air-conditioning (HVAC) operat
content: This study investigates the energy efficiency and operational behaviour of a hydrogen fuel cell electric bus (FCEB) under different fuel cell stack voltage windows, driving cycles, and heating, ventilation and air-conditioning (HVAC) operating modes. A one-dimensional MATLAB/Simulink model coupling a proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) stack, a traction battery, an electric drive and an HVAC subsystem was developed and validated against measured speed data from a real intercity route between Incheon and Seoul, reproducing the measured speed with a coefficient of determination above 0.99 and a maximum local deviation of about 5 %. Two stack voltage windows — Scenario 1 (420–480 V) and Scenario 2 (440–500 V) — were evaluated over three driving cycles: Braunschweig (urban), the World Harmonized Vehicle Cycle (WHVC, mixed) and the European Transient Cycle (ETC, transient heavy-duty), under hot summer (35 °C, 74–75 % relative humidity) and cold winter (−7 °C, 59 % relative humidity) conditions. Of the three factors, the driving cycle had the largest effect: hydrogen consumption over the 700 s window ranged from 0.139 kg in WHVC to 0.257 kg in Braunschweig, a difference of about 85 %, or about 55 % when normalised by the distance covered. The stack voltage window had the smallest effect, Scenario 1 reducing hydrogen consumption by 2.7 %, 2.2 % and 0.9 % for the three cycles while keeping the battery state of charge (SOC) within a narrow band and avoiding deep discharge. HVAC operation fell between the two: under summer conditions at full load it accounted for 22–35 % of the total hydrogen demand with recirculation on and for 14–23 % with fresh-air operation, the latter lowering cumulative HVAC energy by 40–45 %. The results show that auxiliary thermal management influences hydrogen consumption an order of magnitude more strongly than the stack voltage window, and that fuel economy optimisation in fuel cell buses should therefore be treated as an integrated control problem rather than a component-level one.

title: Intelligent Governance of Complex Social Systems: A Hybrid AI–System Dynamics Model for the Simulation and Projection of Sustainable Energy Transition
summary: Amidst growing uncertainty regarding global sustainable development goals and the increasing complexity of social systems, accurately characterizing long-term transition processes driven by the interactions of multiple agents and factors re
content: Amidst growing uncertainty regarding global sustainable development goals and the increasing complexity of social systems, accurately characterizing long-term transition processes driven by the interactions of multiple agents and factors remains a critical challenge. Using China’s energy transition toward carbon neutrality as a proof-of-concept case, this paper constructs a bidirectional coupling framework based on a hybrid Artificial Intelligence–System Dynamics (AI-SD) approach. Within this framework, an axiomatic SD formal system imposes hard constraints on the nonlinear learning processes of the AI, while the nonlinear corrections generated by the AI feed back to modify the system dynamics structure, thereby establishing an iterative cycle of structural constraints, data-driven corrections, and re-imposed structural constraints. Simulation results demonstrate that the hybrid AI-SD model exhibits good comprehensive adaptability in historical fitting and long-term scenario extrapolation, preserving the system feedback structure while characterizing certain nonlinear and time-delay features. The multi-policy synergy scenario, under the conditions set in this paper, shows a high cumulative emission reduction level and exhibits a relatively coordinated characteristic between emission reduction effects and comprehensive social costs. Model-based sensitivity and attribution analyses indicate that, within the defined parameter space, cumulative technology investment and energy cost conditions are associated with higher model output sensitivity; the contribution of carbon pricing shows a certain scenario dependence. This study provides a computable axiomatic framework for the deep integration of mechanistic models and data-driven approaches, and offers theoretical reference for long-term energy governance and complex system decision optimization under deep uncertainty.

title: EO‐Driven Carbon Stock and Ecosystem Modeling in Semi‐arid and Urban Transitional Landscapes
summary: Urban landscapes, often dominated by concrete, are increasingly recognized as vital frontiers in the fight against climate change. This chapter maps carbon stocks and sequestration pathways in South Delhi, a rapidly urbanizing semi-arid reg
content: Urban landscapes, often dominated by concrete, are increasingly recognized as vital frontiers in the fight against climate change. This chapter maps carbon stocks and sequestration pathways in South Delhi, a rapidly urbanizing semi-arid region, to illustrate how cities can shift from being carbon sources to resilient carbon sinks. Using multi-temporal satellite imagery (2000, 2013, and 2024), classified with support vector machines (SVM) for accurate land use–land cover (LULC) mapping, and the InVEST carbon storage model, we generated spatially explicit estimates of carbon stocks and fluxes across four major pools: aboveground biomass, belowground biomass, soil organic carbon, and dead organic matter. Results reveal a substantial decline in carbon stocks between 2000 and 2013 due to urban expansion, followed by a notable recovery and net sequestration gain from 2013 to 2024, largely attributable to afforestation and urban greening initiatives. The findings highlight the pivotal role of urban vegetation as a cost-effective, multifunctional carbon sink in mitigating climate change within dense metropolitan environments. Economic valuation using India-specific social cost of carbon further emphasizes the financial benefits of green infrastructure. This research underscores the importance of integrating ecosystem services into urban planning to foster sustainable, climate-resilient cities in semi-arid settings, while contributing region-specific evidence to the global discourse on urban carbon dynamics and carbon-neutrality pathways.

title: Анализ роли результатов Сахалинского эксперимента в достижении углеродной нейтральности Сахалинской области
source: Naučnye trudy/Naučnye trudy: Institut narodnohozâjstvennogo prognozirovaniâ RAN
summary: Россией были приняты конкретные обязательства по сокращению нетто-выбросов парниковых газов, и одним из инструментов достижения данной цели может являться система торговли выбросами. В России на данный момент действует пилотная система торг
content: Россией были приняты конкретные обязательства по сокращению нетто-выбросов парниковых газов, и одним из инструментов достижения данной цели может являться система торговли выбросами. В России на данный момент действует пилотная система торговли выбросами в рамках Сахалинского эксперимента, первый этап которого завершился в 2025 году. В этом же году было объявлено о достижении углеродной нейтральности в Сахалинской области. В статье приводится описание Сахалинской системы торговли выбросами, анализ результатов первого этапа его функционирования, сравнение подходов к участию компаний в эксперименте, анализ данных Кадастра антропогенных выбросов из источников и абсорбции поглотителями парниковых газов Сахалинской области, сравнение с похожими системами региональных японских моделей. Можно сделать вывод, что, несмотря на выдающиеся результаты региона, не стоит торопиться с распространяем данной модели торговли выбросами на всю страну, поскольку начальные условия баланса выбросов, отраслевая принадлежность участников эксперимента могут отличаться от общероссийских. В рамках эксперимента полностью создана инфраструктура для углеродной торговли, однако достижение углеродной нейтральности было достигнуто главным образом за счет пересчета Кадастра.

title: Understanding value diversity in Finnish urban green spaces through IPBES life frames
summary: Cities globally are increasingly adopting nature-based solutions (NBS) to address climate change, mitigate biodiversity loss and enhance the quality of their living environments. However, urban green spaces (UGSs) hold different values for
content: Cities globally are increasingly adopting nature-based solutions (NBS) to address climate change, mitigate biodiversity loss and enhance the quality of their living environments. However, urban green spaces (UGSs) hold different values for different groups and understanding this plurality is essential for planning that better supports local needs. Drawing on the IPBES Life Framework of Values – Living from, in, with and as nature – we explore the plurality of human-nature relationships across three Finnish cities: Turku, Tampere and Lappeenranta. Data were collected through a participatory, map-based survey completed by 2638 respondents, in which participants marked the locations of important nature places and assessed place-based values using Likert-scale statements, which were grouped into UGS profiles using K-means clustering. We employed Xtreme Gradient Boosting to identify how the social, ecological and technological characteristics of the UGSs are associated with each profile. We identified three distinctive UGS profiles: (1) Value Hotspot, where nature is significantly associated with diverse human values; (2) Low-perceived Value, where nature supports a limited range of values; (3) Experiential Value , where, in nature, cultural and personal experiences dominate. Social attributes – particularly UGS users’ activities and perceived importance of the UGS site – were the strongest predictors of profile membership, while ecological and technological characteristics showed limited influence. Findings demonstrate that value-based UGS profiles can offer planners nuanced insights into how urban nature contributes to users’ wellbeing. Integrating such a social value perspective into NBS planning can support more tailored and equitable live experiences to strengthen human-nature interconnectedness.

title: Assessing the sustainability of ecological sanitation in Kabale, Uganda, using an analytical hierarchy process–based approach
source: Journal of Water Sanitation and Hygiene for Development
summary: ABSTRACT Graphical abstract showing the assessment of EcoSan sustainability in Kabale District, Uganda, using a multi-criteria analysis approach based on health, technical, environmental, socio-cultural, economic and financial, and legal an
content: ABSTRACT Graphical abstract showing the assessment of EcoSan sustainability in Kabale District, Uganda, using a multi-criteria analysis approach based on health, technical, environmental, socio-cultural, economic and financial, and legal and institutional criteria. This study evaluated the sustainability of ecological sanitation (EcoSan) systems in Kabale Municipality, Uganda, using a multi-criteria analysis framework based on the analytical hierarchy process (AHP). Although EcoSan is widely promoted as a low-cost sanitation solution, its long-term sustainability remains insufficiently understood in many developing-country contexts. A mixed-methods approach combined household surveys (n = 108), focus group discussions, key informant interviews, field observations, and a literature review. Sustainability criteria and indicators were identified from the literature and validated through a structured stakeholder workshop. The AHP-derived weights were obtained using pairwise comparison matrices, with consistency ratios below 0.1 (consistency ratio < 0.1) ensuring reliability. Sensitivity analysis was conducted to evaluate the robustness of the results. Six dimensions were assessed: health, technical, financial, environmental, socio-cultural, and legal–institutional. Health (18.8%) and technical (18.7%) ranked highest, while legal–institutional aspects (15.0%) ranked lowest. The sustainability index was 79.7%, indicating sustainability but highlighting vulnerabilities in affordability and long-term financial viability. Sustainability is constrained by cost barriers and reliance on external support mechanisms. The study provides a context-sensitive assessment framework and actionable policy insights. Core indicators, including affordability, limited institutional support, low user compliance, inadequate operation and maintenance, and weak monitoring, continue to jeopardize the long-term sustainability of EcoSan.

title: The Spatial Morphology of Future History
summary: Big History characterizes cosmic evolution as a sequence of thresholds where ordered systems—from stars to civilizations—harvest energy to maintain rising complexity. However, standard historical narratives typically terminate at the presen
content: Big History characterizes cosmic evolution as a sequence of thresholds where ordered systems—from stars to civilizations—harvest energy to maintain rising complexity. However, standard historical narratives typically terminate at the present, treating the future as a domain of pure uncertainty. This study proposes that while specific events are unpredictable, the morphological structure of civilization follows a trajectory shaped by the time-invariant constraints of its generalized environment. We introduce Computational Future Historiography (CFH) to map these structural tendencies. Integrating Non-equilibrium Thermodynamics, Network Science, and classical settlement theories, we argue that the Planetary Trap—driven by the rising maintenance costs of complexity—creates structural pressure for a phase transition toward spatial expansion. To model this trajectory, we apply a recursive Civilizational Expansion Cycle (Node-Edge-Hub-Network), which manifests distinct morphologies across cosmological scales due to a shifting Triarchy of Constraints: the depth of gravity wells (Energy), the limits of hardware durability (Matter), and the finite speed of light (Information). At the Solar System scale, the Energy constraint dictates a highly centralized, monocentric structure (Fortress Sol), organizing a dependent industrial periphery around a kinematically calculated Dynamic Heartland in the Mars-Asteroid corridor. As expansion reaches the Local Stellar Neighborhood (R < 50 ly), the Matter constraint (hardware and biological attrition) triggers Logistical Symmetry Breaking, dissolving the monocentric hierarchy into a Polycentric Federation sustained by interstellar percolation via M-dwarf stepping stones. Finally, at the Galactic scale, the Information constraint (light-speed latency) imposes extreme temporal isolation, acting as an evolutionary filter that drives biological speciation and cognitive divergence. The expanding civilization transcends a unitary polity to become a diverse Galactic Neural Network, bound not by synchronous political control, but by the asynchronous exchange of invariant knowledge. This research posits that the future is not a random accumulation of events, but a constrained morphological adaptation to the unforgiving geometry of our cosmic environment.

title: Ceramic Additive Manufacturing: Innovations Driving Net‐Zero Carbon Solutions
summary: Achieving net-zero carbon emissions requires advances in materials and manufacturing technologies that reduce resource consumption and environmental impact. Ceramic additive manufacturing (AM) offers important advantages over conventional m
content: Achieving net-zero carbon emissions requires advances in materials and manufacturing technologies that reduce resource consumption and environmental impact. Ceramic additive manufacturing (AM) offers important advantages over conventional methods by enabling precise control of complex geometries, minimizing waste, and integrating multiple functionalities within a single process. This chapter reviews key innovations in ceramic AM that support carbon neutrality, including multi-material printing, sintering-free processing routes, supportless fabrication techniques, and design optimization through computational tools. Applications are discussed in energy conversion and storage, hydrogen production, environmental remediation, and carbon capture, where AM enhances efficiency, durability, and sustainability. These developments underline the potential of ceramic AM not only to improve performance in demanding environments but also to contribute directly to decarbonization and the establishment of circular manufacturing pathways.

title: Porous Carbon Prepared from Coal Tar Pitch was Doped with N/S to Prepare Supercapacitors
summary: Abstract Coal tar pitch (CTP), a hazardous coal-chemical byproduct, requires high-value recycling for sustainable energy applications, yet precise structural and electrochemical regulation of pitch-derived carbon materials remains challengi
content: Abstract Coal tar pitch (CTP), a hazardous coal-chemical byproduct, requires high-value recycling for sustainable energy applications, yet precise structural and electrochemical regulation of pitch-derived carbon materials remains challenging. Herein, a facile postcarbonization N/S codoping strategy via thiourea-assisted hydrothermal treatment is developed to optimize porous carbon for supercapacitors. Traditional one-step inorganic doping severely damages carbon frameworks and restricts pore development, while hydrothermal-first preparation also delivers inferior porous structures. To overcome these drawbacks, we adopt a sequential strategy: preconstructing hierarchical porous carbon skeleton followed by thiourea-mediated N/S doping. This method well preserves carbon integrity and porous features, overcoming the inherent deficiencies of conventional doping routes. Combined SEM, XRD, and Raman results verify that this strategy enhances graphitization by eliminating amorphous carbon while maintaining intact porous architecture. The optimized PC–NS–2 sample possesses an ultrahigh micropore proportion of 97% and a large specific surface area of 1426.73 m2/g. It achieves a specific capacitance of 307 F g–1 at 0.5 A/g and maintains 93.98% capacitance retention after 10,000 cycles at 5 A/g, showing superior electrochemical kinetics and cycling stability. The assembled symmetric supercapacitor delivers an energy density of 27.8 Wh/kg at 0.5 A/g. Such excellent performance benefits from well-preserved hierarchical pores, optimized graphitization and improved conductivity brought by N/S codoping. This work provides an efficient structure-stable doping strategy for CTP high-value utilization and offers a feasible reference for advanced carbon electrode design.

title: Concept of sustainable territories: BREEAM and a resource-based economy analysis
summary: Sustainable territorial development ensures the harmonious development of society, creating societal welfare, meeting the existing demands of its residents while not endangering the future generations. Sustainable use of resources, circular
content: Sustainable territorial development ensures the harmonious development of society, creating societal welfare, meeting the existing demands of its residents while not endangering the future generations. Sustainable use of resources, circular economy and efficient urban planning help to ensure harmonious territorial development. International agreements, such as the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals, aim at reducing poverty, improving education, managing water resources in a sustainable way, and preserving biodiversity. The purpose of the study is to determine the similarities and differences between J. Fresco’s System and BREEAM certification evaluation criteria. Although utopian, this research finds that J. Fresco’s System Design has similarities with the BREEAM assessment criteria. Both place a strong emphasis on urban planning and the use of renewable energy sources. However, there is a fundamental difference between these systems – BREEAM is a standardized assessment method that is used to certify specific buildings or projects according to defined criteria, while J. Fresco’s System is an economic vision that proposes to transform society by eliminating money, competition, and overconsumption. Article in Lithuanian. Tvarių teritorijų samprata: BREEAM ir ištekliais grįstos ekonomikos požiūrių analizė Santrauka Tvari teritorijų plėtra užtikrina darnią visuomenės plėtrą, sukuriant socialinę gerovę, tenkinant dabartinius žmonių poreikius ir nekeliant pavojaus ateities kartoms. Tvarus išteklių naudojimas, žiedinė ekonomika ir efektyvus miestų planavimas padeda užtikrinti darnių teritorijų plėtrą. Tarptautiniai susitarimai, tokie kaip Jungtinių Tautų darnaus vystymosi tikslai, apima skurdo mažinimą, švietimo gerinimą, tvarų vandens išteklių valdymą ir biologinės įvairovės išsaugojimą. Tyrimo tikslas – nustatyti panašumus ir skirtumus tarp Ž. Fresko ideologijos ir BREEAM sertifikavimo vertinimo kriterijų. Atlikus tyrimą nustatyta, kad, nors Ž. Fresko ideologija yra utopinė, ji turi panašumų su BREEAM vertinimo kriterijais – didelis dėmesys skiriamas miestų planavimui ir atsinaujinančiųjų energijos šaltinių naudojimui. Tačiau tarp šių sistemų yra esminis skirtumas – BREEAM yra standartizuota vertinimo sistema, kuri yra naudojama konkretiems pastatams ar projektams sertifikuoti pagal apibrėžtus kriterijus, o Ž. Fresko idėja yra ekonominė vizija, siūlanti pertvarkyti visuomenę, panaikinant pinigus, konkurenciją ir perteklinį vartojimą. Reikšminiai žodžiai: ištekliais grįsta ekonomika, tvarus miestas, tvarios užstatytos teritorijos, darnus miestų vystymasis.

title: Shadow Pricing Ecosystem Services in Boreal Forests
summary: Abstract Boreal forests jointly produce marketed goods and non-market ecosystem services, generating unavoidable trade-offs. We estimate shadow prices with the directional distance function (R. G. Chambers et al. 1996), endogenizing the dir
content: Abstract Boreal forests jointly produce marketed goods and non-market ecosystem services, generating unavoidable trade-offs. We estimate shadow prices with the directional distance function (R. G. Chambers et al. 1996), endogenizing the directional vector and correcting for sampling variation via bootstrap methods. Using a county-by-year panel of Swedish forests, we find that shadow prices vary spatially and temporally yet remain generally low, implying modest opportunity costs for improving biodiversity and carbon sequestration relative to timber. Morishima elasticities further characterize substitution possibilities and least-cost paths to better environmental outcomes. The results indicate unexploited scope for conservation policy in boreal systems.

title: Engineering cooperative oxide interfaces to regulate carbon dioxide adsorption and electrocatalytic selectivity
source: Journal of Colloid and Interface Science
summary: Carbon dioxide electrocatalysts are conventionally designed to optimize reactant adsorption and conversion at the same catalytic surface. Here, we introduce an alternative design concept in which these functions are distributed across a nan
content: Carbon dioxide electrocatalysts are conventionally designed to optimize reactant adsorption and conversion at the same catalytic surface. Here, we introduce an alternative design concept in which these functions are distributed across a nanoscale oxide interface. A nanocoating is integrated with zinc oxide nanorods to create interfacial sites that favour carbon dioxide adsorption while preserving the underlying zinc oxide centers responsible for its electrochemical conversion. Structural, surface, and in-situ spectroscopic characterisation reveals that the nanocoating preserves the zinc oxide crystal structure and nanorod morphology while modifying the local surface environment and promoting oxygen-vacancy formation. Density functional theory calculations provide an atomistic picture of this interface, identifying favourable interfacial aluminum‑oxygen configurations that strengthen carbon dioxide binding and support increased carbon dioxide availability near the zinc oxide active centers. Importantly, this interfacial regulation translates into a marked shift in the competition between carbon dioxide reduction and hydrogen evolution: whereas bare zinc oxide progressively loses carbon monoxide selectivity at increasingly cathodic potentials, the modified interface sustains carbon monoxide formation while suppressing the competing hydrogen evolution reaction. These findings establish an electrocatalyst design principle in which molecular adsorption and catalytic conversion are promoted by different but cooperating components of the same nanoscale architecture. Rather than altering the bulk catalyst to optimize its intrinsic activity, engineering the local reaction environment redirects competing electrochemical pathways towards carbon dioxide conversion, providing a general strategy for controlling electrocatalytic selectivity through functional differentiation at catalytic interfaces.

title: Does low-carbon transition policy improve water–energy–land–food nexus performance considering ESG practice?
summary: As the global climate crisis intensifies, the interplay between low-carbon transition policies and the sustainable management of critical resources has gained increasing scholarly and policy interest. This study investigates whether the imp
content: As the global climate crisis intensifies, the interplay between low-carbon transition policies and the sustainable management of critical resources has gained increasing scholarly and policy interest. This study investigates whether the implementation of low-carbon transition policies improves the performance of the water–energy–land–food (WELF) nexus in the context of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices in China. Drawing on provincial panel data from 2007 to 2023, we employ fixed effects models, heterogeneity tests, mediation effect analysis, and a PSM–DID approach to evaluate the net impact and underlying mechanisms. The results reveal that low-carbon policies significantly enhance the coupling and coordination degree of the WELF nexus, particularly in regions with stronger ESG governance and higher environmental regulation intensity. By 2023, the regional average coupling degree had increased by 2.021% compared to 2007. During the 17-year period, the mean coupling degree across all provinces and municipalities was 0.947. Mechanism analysis indicates that improvements in energy efficiency, industrial upgrading, and technological innovation are key pathways through which low-carbon policies strengthen nexus performance while aligning with ESG objectives. However, the effects vary by regional economic development level, population size, regulatory context, and market openness. These findings underscore the importance of integrating ESG principles into policy design to maximize synergies between decarbonization and holistic resource management. The study provides empirical evidence to support more targeted and adaptive low-carbon and ESG governance strategies that foster coordinated progress towards sustainability and climate goals.

title: Being Granular, Becoming Sustainable:
summary: This article examines the integration of digitization and environmental concerns in digital agriculture from the perspective of actors in smart farming in Switzerland. Those actors, previously unconnected to farming, promote the use of gran
content: This article examines the integration of digitization and environmental concerns in digital agriculture from the perspective of actors in smart farming in Switzerland. Those actors, previously unconnected to farming, promote the use of granular data to achieve more sustainable practices. Considering granularity as a practitioner-made achievement rather than a technical property alone, I draw on interviews and ethnographic observations, and rely on material-semiotic insights from STS (Law, 2008; Mol, 1999; Lien & Law, 2011) to examine how granularity data is brought into existence through heterogeneous practices. I first analyze how the connection between digital agriculture and more sustainable practices is operated as a motto, an aspirational principle that draws from different sources and comparisons. I then show how the production and interpretation of granular data depend on experimental infrastructures, interdisciplinary collaboration, and ongoing human interpretation, all of which contribute to the existence of granularity while enacting specific definitions of sustainability.

title: Exploring bias filters as a source evaluation tool
summary: Today's complex, algorithmically-driven information landscape can be difficult to navigate. While media literacy skills are important for negotiating this complexity, a pedagogical focus on misinformation and fact-checking can have the unin
content: Today's complex, algorithmically-driven information landscape can be difficult to navigate. While media literacy skills are important for negotiating this complexity, a pedagogical focus on misinformation and fact-checking can have the unintended effect of increasing already widespread cynicism, including among young people. In this exploratory study, we introduced college students to a new pedagogical concept: bias filters. Bias filters are aspects of the information creation process that help to reduce bias in the final product. The findings suggest that bias filters have considerable promise as an instructional tool, encouraging students to approach information sources with a more nuanced, less cynical perspective. Future potential considerations and implications for bias filters as an instructional inclusion are discussed.

title: Lactate‐Depleting Nanotherapy Reprograms the Immunometabolic Microenvironment to Overcome Biofilm Tolerance in Implant‐Associated Infections
summary: Biofilm formation in implant-associated infections (IAIs) establishes an immunosuppressive microenvironment while conferring profound antibiotic tolerance. Through multi-omics profiling of clinical IAI samples, we identify lactate as a key
content: Biofilm formation in implant-associated infections (IAIs) establishes an immunosuppressive microenvironment while conferring profound antibiotic tolerance. Through multi-omics profiling of clinical IAI samples, we identify lactate as a key metabolite associated with immunosuppression within the biofilm-associated microenvironment of IAIs. Guided by this insight, we engineer a nanotherapeutic platform (LMVM) comprising vacancy-engineered hollow magnetite nanoparticles (VE-HMN) coloaded with lactate oxidase (LOX) and metronidazole (MNZ). By depleting lactate, LMVM remodels the immunosuppressive microenvironment and restores antimicrobial immunity, thereby highlighting lactate as an immunometabolic regulator in biofilm-associated infections. Simultaneously, lactate oxidation intensifies local hypoxia, which redirects bacterial metabolism to activate MNZ against tolerant subpopulations while suppressing staphyloxanthin (STX)-dependent antioxidant defenses. As a result, this immunometabolism-guided nanotherapy achieves robust biofilm eradication in murine IAI models and promotes tissue repair. Collectively, these findings identify lactate-mediated immunosuppression as a therapeutically actionable feature of biofilm-associated infections and support a clinically guided materials strategy that couples immunometabolic microenvironment remodeling with the eradication of antibiotic-tolerant biofilms.

title: Epistemic jurisdictions and standardized objectivity: observing regulatory science in nanotechnology in Argentina and Brazil
source: Tapuya Latin American Science Technology and Society
summary: This article examines regulatory science as a co-production of technical and policy reasoning about the environmental and health risks of emerging technologies in Latin America. Focusing on nanotechnology in health applications (drugs and m
content: This article examines regulatory science as a co-production of technical and policy reasoning about the environmental and health risks of emerging technologies in Latin America. Focusing on nanotechnology in health applications (drugs and medical devices) in Argentina and Brazil, the article explores how scientific knowledge is mobilized to define standards for nano-risk within two national regulatory bodies: the National Administration of Drugs, Food and Medical Technology (ANMAT) and the National Health Surveillance Agency (ANVISA). Drawing on document analysis, interviews with regulatory officials and experts, and participatory research workshops, the study addresses the influence of international organizations (FDA, EMA, OECD, and ISO) on local regulatory science, analyzing the mediating mechanisms through which that influence operates. The article discusses how the objectivity of expert judgment becomes standardized under regulatory reliance approaches, and how epistemic and normative authority is consequently configured in these semi-peripheral contexts. The analysis contributes to Latin American STS debates by bringing the concepts of epistemic jurisdictions, subordinate integration, field-network, and emulation into dialogue with one another.

title: ТРАНСФОРМАЦІЯ АГРОБІЗНЕСУ УКРАЇНИ В УМОВАХ ЄВРОІНТЕГРАЦІЇ: СИНЕРГІЯ КЛІМАТИЧНОЇ ПОЛІТИКИ ТА КОНЦЕПЦІЇ ESG
summary: Global climate change and European integration require the fundamental transformation of Ukraine's agricultural sector toward climate neutrality and low-carbon development. Following the adoption of the Law of Ukraine «On the Basic Principl
content: Global climate change and European integration require the fundamental transformation of Ukraine's agricultural sector toward climate neutrality and low-carbon development. Following the adoption of the Law of Ukraine «On the Basic Principles of State Climate Policy» No. 3991-IX, agribusiness faces the necessity of adapting to tight environmental standards, risks of the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), and requirements of international investors. The objective of the study is to substantiate the transformation processes within Ukraine's agribusiness under conditions of European integration through the synergy of state climate policy and the ESG concept to attract international investment for «green» post-war recovery. The study employs methods of systemic, comparative, and regulatory analysis to examine climate legislation, alongside synthesis and structural-functional methods to categorize key stakeholders and analyze market-based decarbonization tools. Four key dimensions of agricultural changes driven by new legislation were identified: cross-sectoral integration of climate goals, regulatory formalization of circular economy and nature-based solutions, implementation of emissions monitoring and reporting, and adaptation to climate risks. The study establishes that ESG criteria serve as a practical passport for corporate compliance with the European Green Deal and accessing green finance. The scientific novelty lies in the comprehensive conceptualization of the synergistic interaction between national climate legislation and ESG benchmarks as an integrated framework for the low-carbon transition of agribusiness. The practical significance is demonstrated through the mechanism of monetizing sustainable farming practices via the Agricultural Climate Change Adaptation Program, allowing producers to generate additional revenue by issuing and trading carbon certificates. The article provides the relevant calculations.

title: Harmonization of biogas, greenhouse gases, water quality, and energy consumption in sidestream systems using computational assessment
summary: ABSTRACT Graphical summary of the study. Four anaerobic digestion configurations - conventional anaerobic digestion, thermal hydrolysis combined with conventional digestion, an anaerobic membrane bioreactor configuration, and the fully inte
content: ABSTRACT Graphical summary of the study. Four anaerobic digestion configurations - conventional anaerobic digestion, thermal hydrolysis combined with conventional digestion, an anaerobic membrane bioreactor configuration, and the fully integrated configuration - are evaluated by plant-wide simulation across food-waste mixing ratios. Four indicators (specific methane production, sidestream load to mainstream, greenhouse gas emissions and energy footprint) are normalised and combined into a single composite Sustainability WWTP Index. This study evaluated the sustainability of four anaerobic digestion (AD) configurations, namely conventional anaerobic digester (CAD), thermal hydrolysis coupled with CAD (THP + CAD), CAD integrated with an anaerobic membrane bioreactor (AnMBR), and a fully integrated THP + CAD + AnMBR system. Process simulation and response surface methodology (RSM) were applied to assess system performance under varying food waste (FW) ratios. the sustainability WWTP Index (SWI) was developed by integrating specific methane production (SMP), sidestream load to mainstream (SLM), greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and energy footprint (ENF). Advanced configurations enhanced methane production at moderate FW ratios. However, synergy decreased at 50% FW, where THP + CAD + AnMBR's SMP (11.5) fell below the CAD baseline (11.8). THP + CAD achieved the most consistently favourable SWI balance, maintaining a 100% above-median frequency up to 25% FW. The AnMBR-based systems exhibited higher volatility and increased the GHG footprint by approximately 4.5%. Ammonia rose with food waste addition, yet free ammonia stayed below inhibitory levels in all scenarios. Optimization indicated that for the THP + CAD + AnMBR configuration, a 0.35 bypass ratio and a 50-day SRT maximized the SWI. These findings show that AD configuration performance depends on the operating regime, which the SWI makes explicit.

title: Transport cost-benefit analysis: critical evaluation and improvement
summary: Cost–benefit analysis (CBA) remains the dominant framework for the ex ante evaluation of transport policies and infrastructure investments, grounded in welfare economics and aimed at maximizing aggregate social welfare. However, a growing b
content: Cost–benefit analysis (CBA) remains the dominant framework for the ex ante evaluation of transport policies and infrastructure investments, grounded in welfare economics and aimed at maximizing aggregate social welfare. However, a growing body of literature questions whether CBA adequately captures the multidimensional objectives of contemporary transport policy, including effectiveness, efficiency, and equity. This paper addresses this debate by systematically identifying and structuring criticisms of CBA in transport, drawing on a scoping review of 75 publications and insights from two expert workshops involving 16 specialists from multiple disciplines. The analysis categorizes criticisms into four groups: (1) fundamental limitations of CBA; (2) shortcomings in practical application; (3) issues related to debatable policy questions; and (4) decision-making challenges.
