title: Exploring climate change impacts through awareness, incidence, and adaptation strategies among farmers in Mid-Illovo, KwaZulu-Natal Province, South Africa: a principal component analysis
summary: This study assessed the impacts of climate change on smallholder farmers and their adaptation strategies in the Mid-Illovo region, KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. Using a descriptive research design, 60 farmers were selected randomly from 250
content: This study assessed the impacts of climate change on smallholder farmers and their adaptation strategies in the Mid-Illovo region, KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. Using a descriptive research design, 60 farmers were selected randomly from 250 from which data were collected through a structured questionnaire and analyzed using means, frequency counts, percentages, probit analysis, and principal component analysis. The results show that more than 70% of the farmers are aware of the incidence of climate changes and engaged in crop, water, nutrient, livestock, and weather-smart practices. The results of the analysis of adoption of climate change practices reveal that age (Z = 1.671, p = 0.095), household income (Z = 1.705, p = 0.088), awareness of adaptation practices (Z= 2.562, p = 0.010), and climate change incidence parameters (Z= 2.305, p = 0.021), were significant factors. The Principal Component Analysis method identified five components, namely, Factor 1 (Eco-physiological Stress), Factor 2 (Socioeconomic Fragility), Factor 3 (Climatic and Soil instability), Factor 4 (Atmospheric Disruption) and Factor 5 (Seasonal Extremes and Livelihood Impact) and accounted for a cumulative variance of 55.63%. The study recommends the provision of climate information and early warning systems, and promotion of climate-resilient agricultural practices.

title: Navigating Institutional Landscapes: Grassroots Sustainability in Library Contexts
summary: Like many institutions and organizations, libraries face complications stemming from the different values of formal administration and the individuals doing the work. Sustainability and climate crisis work is one area where these conflictin
content: Like many institutions and organizations, libraries face complications stemming from the different values of formal administration and the individuals doing the work. Sustainability and climate crisis work is one area where these conflicting priorities can come into play. Administrative leaders often have their own agenda, goals and actions; they shift to a new institution and with that, values, actions and services shift in tandem, directly affecting individuals' work and organizational culture. This article provides a brief history of sustainability work in libraries, explores the complications of conventional management, and offers alternative examples of grassroots leadership for climate action work in libraries.

title: Can electric buses encourage greater public transport use? The role of the green halo effect
summary: The electrification of urban bus fleets is widely promoted as a strategy to reduce emissions and enhance the sustainability of public transport systems. Beyond environmental benefits, electric buses may also influence user perceptions and t
content: The electrification of urban bus fleets is widely promoted as a strategy to reduce emissions and enhance the sustainability of public transport systems. Beyond environmental benefits, electric buses may also influence user perceptions and travel behavior. This study investigates how the introduction of electric buses in Thessaloniki affects both actual public transport usage and intentions to increase future use, adopting a holistic approach that considers both users and non-users. Building on existing electric bus adoption models, we extend the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) by introducing the green halo effect, capturing the positive spillover of electric bus deployment on the overall image of public transport. The framework also incorporates green self-identity, attitudes, social norms, and satisfaction-related perceptions. Data were collected through an online survey of Thessaloniki residents (N = 474), including both electric bus users (N = 323) and non-users (N = 151). For users, the model examines changes in usage frequency, while for non-users it analyzes intentions to adopt public transport. Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) is applied to test relationships among psychological constructs and behavioral outcomes, complemented by Necessary Condition Analysis (NCA) to identify critical limiting factors for intended modal shift. Results indicate that for current users, physical ride quality is a necessary condition for satisfaction, while the green halo effect independently increases usage frequency. For non-users, exploratory findings suggest that the green halo effect emerges as the strongest model-based predictor and primary limiting factor for future adoption within this sample, overriding general attitudes toward public transport. These findings highlight the potential of fleet electrification to act as a facilitator for behavioral change regarding increasing public transport use.

title: A LoRa-based IoT Monitoring System for Hybrid Solar–Wind Energy Applications Under Constrained Connectivity
source: Technical Education Science/Giáo dục Kỹ thuật
summary: The rapid expansion of solar and wind energy systems has increased the demand for reliable monitoring solutions, particularly in regions where network infrastructure is limited or unstable. In Vietnam, most existing monitoring approaches pr
content: The rapid expansion of solar and wind energy systems has increased the demand for reliable monitoring solutions, particularly in regions where network infrastructure is limited or unstable. In Vietnam, most existing monitoring approaches primarily target single-source renewable installations and rely on WiFi or cellular networks, which are often unavailable in remote hybrid deployment scenarios. To address this limitation, this paper presents a low-cost IoT (Internet of Things)-based monitoring system for hybrid solar–wind energy applications, with an emphasis on reliable data acquisition under constrained connectivity conditions. The proposed system utilizes an ESP32 microcontroller integrated with a LoRa communication module to support long-range wireless transmission, while a local data buffering mechanism is employed to maintain data continuity during temporary network outages. Key electrical and environmental parameters, including voltage, current, temperature, and wind speed, are continuously monitored. Collected measurement data are stored in an InfluxDB time-series database and visualized using Grafana dashboards for real-time and historical analysis. Experimental validation demonstrates stable LoRa communication over distances of approximately 400 m in urban environments and up to 700 m in open areas, as well as consistent monitoring performance during WiFi interruptions and varying renewable input conditions. The proposed system provides a practical and reliable monitoring solution for hybrid renewable energy systems operating under limited connectivity and establishes a foundation for future extensions toward advanced data analytics and remote supervision.

title: From Waste to Wealth: The Economic Case for Valorising the United Arab Emirates’ Agricultural and Food-Processing Biomass Residues Energy Production, Carbon-Credit Revenue, and Net-Zero Contribution Across Three Deployment Scenarios
source: Emirati Journal of Business Economics & Social Studies
summary: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) generates an estimated 8–12 million tonnes of agriculture- and food-related organic residue each year, a stream presently treated overwhelmingly as a disposal liability rather than an economic asset. This arti
content: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) generates an estimated 8–12 million tonnes of agriculture- and food-related organic residue each year, a stream presently treated overwhelmingly as a disposal liability rather than an economic asset. This article makes the economic case for valorising that residue and argues three propositions. First, the costliest element of any biomass value chain—collection and logistics—already exists in the UAE, because municipal waste utilities, a commercial waste-to-energy facility, agricultural extension services, source-segregation regulation, and the region’s pioneering permitted carbon-dioxide storage infrastructure are all operational. Second, three deployment scenarios—energy-only, carbon-only, and a hybrid carbon-plus-energy pathway—are evaluated for their annual contribution to national electricity supply, carbon-credit revenue, gross domestic product (GDP), and the UAE’s Net Zero by 2050 commitment. The realistic energy potential is approximately 2.2–3.0 terawatt-hours per year, equivalent to roughly 1.5–2.0% of national electricity demand, while permanent carbon removal under the hybrid pathway reaches approximately 3.6–4.3 million tonnes of carbon dioxide per year. Third, the hybrid pathway is shown to stack two high-value revenue streams—electricity sales and durable carbon-removal credits—generating an estimated US$0.85–1.1 billion in direct annual revenue, with a broader economic footprint, including avoided disposal costs, gas-export substitution, and fertiliser import substitution, plausibly reaching US$2–3 billion per year. The carbon-credit component constitutes a genuinely new, foreign-exchange-earning In-Country Value revenue stream aligned with national diversification objectives. The article concludes that the hybrid pathway represents the optimal long-term strategy and recommends a staged deployment sequence gated on carbon-credit price thresholds and storage access. Keywords: biomass valorisation, bioenergy, biochar, carbon credits, BECCS, In-Country Value, Net Zero 2050, circular economy, United Arab Emirates

title: Hierarchical upscaling forest biomass mapping by fusing UAV-LiDAR, calibrated GEDI, and ALOS-2 PALSAR-2 data
summary: Accurate estimation of forest aboveground biomass (AGB) is crucial for understanding the global carbon cycle and supporting carbon neutrality. However, conventional methods relying on single remote sensing sources are often constrained by s
content: Accurate estimation of forest aboveground biomass (AGB) is crucial for understanding the global carbon cycle and supporting carbon neutrality. However, conventional methods relying on single remote sensing sources are often constrained by signal saturation resulting from limited vertical detection capability and by their limited ability to characterize changes in AGB across large-scale subtropical regions characterized by complex topography and high spatial heterogeneity. To address this, we proposed a hierarchical multi-source inversion framework integrating unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) light detection and ranging (LiDAR), Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation (GEDI), Advanced Land Observing Satellite-2 (ALOS-2) Phased Array type L-band Synthetic Aperture Radar-2 (PALSAR-2), and Sentinel-2. The framework employs a three-step upscaling strategy to progressively transfer inversion accuracy. First, a high-precision local reference layer was generated using UAV LiDAR and field plots to serve as reliable ground truth. Next, this layer was used to correct GEDI L4A products using machine learning models, and then the approach with best performance was selected for footprint-level estimation. Finally, corrected GEDI footprints were combined with PALSAR-2 structural metrics and Sentinel-2 spectral features to produce a wall-to-wall AGB map with resolution of 30 m. Results showed that UAV-based correction significantly improved GEDI accuracy, yielding an R2 of 0.78 and a root mean square error (RMSE) of 19.97 Mg/ha, the total uncertainty with pixel-level was controlled within 36.26 Mg/ha. In conclusion, the proposed framework, leveraging physical mechanism feature guidance, offers a novel and robust strategy for the high-precision inversion of forest AGB across large-scale with complex topography and high spatial heterogeneity.

title: On Gaussian–Bessel Integrals in Diffusion‐Based Wind‐Turbine Wake Models
summary: ABSTRACT The diffusion wake model provides an analytical description of turbine‐wake evolution from a top‐hat profile in the near wake to a self‐similar Gaussian profile in the far wake. The main formulation of the model involves an integra
content: ABSTRACT The diffusion wake model provides an analytical description of turbine‐wake evolution from a top‐hat profile in the near wake to a self‐similar Gaussian profile in the far wake. The main formulation of the model involves an integral containing the product of linear, Gaussian, and modified Bessel‐function terms. This integral is closely related to the Marcum ‐function and is commonly evaluated using series representations, limiting its analytical tractability. In this short communication, we develop a compact closed‐form approximation for this integral in terms of the error function. Comparisons with numerical quadrature show multi‐order‐of‐magnitude accuracy over the parameter range considered, with errors at least two orders of magnitude smaller than the corresponding function values. The approximation is then used to revisit the diffusion wake model and refine both its main formulation and its momentum‐conservation condition. In addition, the approximation is combined with recursive properties of the Marcum ‐function to obtain a compact representation of the generalized Marcum ‐function. The resulting formulation offers a simple and accurate alternative to series‐based evaluations while preserving the analytical structure of the original wake model.

title: Extremophilic microorganisms colonization of acidic historic ink with precipitation, dissolution and translocation of jarosite
summary: Iron gall ink (IGI), used in Europe from the 12th to 19th centuries, was made from iron(II) sulfate, tannin-rich plant extracts and organic binders. Polyphenol reactions yield brown iron complexes that darken on oxygen exposure; IGI typical
content: Iron gall ink (IGI), used in Europe from the 12th to 19th centuries, was made from iron(II) sulfate, tannin-rich plant extracts and organic binders. Polyphenol reactions yield brown iron complexes that darken on oxygen exposure; IGI typically has pH 2-4. In some ancient documents, jarosite crystals formed in the ink, causing text to fade. Reproduction attempts reached no conclusive explanation; wetting-drying cycles are considered the main trigger. A 17th-century Italian manuscript with discolored IGI was examined by micro-Raman spectroscopy, SEM-EDS and metagenomics. The hydroxy-sulfate mineral jarosite (potassium-, sodium- and hydronium-variety) was identified as the cause: dendritic precipitates and pseudo-rhombohedral crystals showing dissolution, associated with fungi and bacteria. Jarosite was closely associated with fungi and bacteria. Acidophilic fungi ( Geotrichum, Coniochaeta ) mobilized elements inside and outside inked areas. Jarosite formation reflects interconnected inorganic-organic processes, iron redox cycling, organic-iron complexation and pH decrease below 3.0, mainly non-biological, with fungi driving dissolution and reprecipitation.

title: Determining the values of soil‐mediated contributions to people: A comparative European perspective
summary: Abstract Soil health is a fundamental element underpinning terrestrial ecosystems, yet it is persistently threatened by the ongoing process of land degradation, leading to detrimental impacts on human well‐being. However, there is a paucity
content: Abstract Soil health is a fundamental element underpinning terrestrial ecosystems, yet it is persistently threatened by the ongoing process of land degradation, leading to detrimental impacts on human well‐being. However, there is a paucity of research on the extent to which humans are dependent on soils and the societal values attributed to their vital functions. In accordance with the Intergovernmental Science‐Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services (IPBES) valuation framework, we conducted a comprehensive assessment of the values and preferences attributed to soil‐mediated contributions to humans. The study employed a multifaceted approach, incorporating a socio‐cultural valuation, a discrete choice experiment and a landscape‐preferences assessment. With sample respondents from Denmark, Spain and Ireland, the objective of the study was to elicit the values and determinants of value from these countries and compare them across different geographical regions and methods. Specifically, we aimed to evaluate the extent to which socio‐demographic characteristics, knowledge, attitudes, behaviours and underlying value constructs influence these valuation outcomes. The results of the analysis indicate more subtle differences in the values and preferences between the countries than for the determinants of the values. While socio‐demographic characteristics exhibited certain trends in determining values, significant disparities in knowledge, attitudes, behaviours and underlying value constructs persisted, underscoring the intricacies and variability that shape values for soil‐mediated contributions to people. While site‐ or region‐level approaches may offer a nuanced understanding, the results of this study provide a foundation for decision and policy makers to integrate the values and leverage their determinants, thereby fostering broader acceptance and enhancing the effectiveness of soil policies. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.

title: Enerji Tüketimi ve Yenilenebilir Enerjinin Türkiye’de Sera Gazı Emisyonlarına Etkisi: ARDL ve Bayesyen Analiz
summary: Sera gazı emisyonları, iklim değişikliği ve çevresel sürdürülebilirlik tartışmalarının merkezinde yer almakta olup enerji yapısındaki dönüşümün çevresel sonuçlarını değerlendirmede temel göstergelerden biri olarak kabul edilmektedir. Çalışm
content: Sera gazı emisyonları, iklim değişikliği ve çevresel sürdürülebilirlik tartışmalarının merkezinde yer almakta olup enerji yapısındaki dönüşümün çevresel sonuçlarını değerlendirmede temel göstergelerden biri olarak kabul edilmektedir. Çalışmada, 1992-2021 dönemi Türkiye verileri kullanılarak enerji tüketimi (ET) ve yenilenebilir enerji tüketiminin (YET) sera gazı emisyonları (SGE) üzerindeki etkileri ARDL modeli ile Bayesyen regresyon yaklaşımı çerçevesinde karşılaştırmalı olarak analiz edilmiştir. Bayesyen yöntemde hem bilgi vermeyen hem de bilgi veren önsel dağılımlar kullanılmış; bilgi veren önseller Türkiye ile benzer yapısal özellikler taşıdığı değerlendirilen Meksika, İspanya ve Polonya verilerinden oluşturulmuştur. ARDL sınır testi sonuçları, değişkenler arasında uzun dönemli eşbütünleşme ilişkisi bulunduğunu göstermektedir. ARDL bulgularına göre enerji tüketimi kısa ve uzun dönemde sera gazı emisyonlarını artırırken, yenilenebilir enerji tüketimi kısa dönemde emisyonları azaltıcı etki göstermektedir. Bayesyen analiz sonuçları da enerji tüketiminin emisyon artırıcı etkisini desteklemekte, yenilenebilir enerji tüketiminin etkisinin ise kullanılan önsel bilgi setine göre farklılaşabildiğini ortaya koymaktadır. Bulgular, Türkiye’de fosil yakıtlara dayalı enerji talebinin çevresel baskıyı artırdığını, yenilenebilir enerji yatırımlarının ise emisyonların sınırlandırılmasında önemli bir araç olduğunu göstermektedir.

title: Mechanisms of rare earth elements dispersion from the Jiaping ion-adsorption rare earth deposit, Guangxi, China: Implications for exploration
summary: Ion-adsorption rare earth deposits (IAREDs) supply most of the world’s heavy rare earth elements (HREE), yet the downstream dispersion and phase partitioning of rare earth elements (REE) remain poorly constrained. We analyzed the operationa
content: Ion-adsorption rare earth deposits (IAREDs) supply most of the world’s heavy rare earth elements (HREE), yet the downstream dispersion and phase partitioning of rare earth elements (REE) remain poorly constrained. We analyzed the operationally dissolved fraction (<0.45 μm), suspended particulate matter (SPM), and bed sediment along a 4.5-km stream draining the unmined Jiaping deposit in Guangxi, South China. The results of this study show that REE concentrations exhibit downstream attenuation across all media, with sediments (98.44–255.31 ppm) and SPM (66.28–182.56 ppm) constituting primary reservoirs over the dissolved phase (0.53–1.21 ppb). As pH increased from 5.28 to 7.04, thermodynamic modeling indicated a shift from free REE 3+ ions toward carbonate complexes. This shift promoted preferential HREE association with Fe-(oxy)hydroxides and particle aggregation, producing relative light REE enrichment in the dissolved and suspended fractions and HREE enrichment in bed sediment. SPM δCe increased from 0.89 to 1.55, consistent with oxidative Ce scavenging and aggregation of Ce-rich colloids. Bed sediment retained closer correspondence to the parent granite and regolith in (La/Sm) N and δEu. These results support two concurrent pathways: detrital transport preserves source signatures in bed sediment, whereas aqueous–colloidal transport modifies dissolved and suspended signatures. Under dry-season baseflow conditions, bed sediment was the most reliable sampling medium, providing a mechanistic basis for regional IARED exploration.

title: Insights into Electrolyte Effects on Interfacial Kinetics and Transport in Porous Redox Flow Battery Electrodes: A Multiparadigm Modelling Study
summary: Redox flow batteries (RFBs) have emerged as promising candidates for large-scale energy storage owing to their decoupled energy and power densities. Electrolyte formulation plays a key role in determining the electrochemical performance of
content: Redox flow batteries (RFBs) have emerged as promising candidates for large-scale energy storage owing to their decoupled energy and power densities. Electrolyte formulation plays a key role in determining the electrochemical performance of RFBs, influencing interfacial kinetics and transport within porous electrodes. Herein, we develop a multiscale modelling framework to investigate the coupled effects of the electrolyte concentration (Methyl Viologen (MV) and NaCl) and the fibrous 3D microstructure on the porous transport and electrochemical kinetics in organic RFBs using a kinetic Monte Carlo model. We link this interfacial kinetics to the advection-diffusion transport in stochastically generated carbon felt electrode microstructures through Lattice Boltzmann Method simulations via an interpolation-based coupling. We use two performance descriptors, the fibre-averaged rate of potential loss and convective area fraction, to quantify the kinetics and transport effects, along with their interplay. While increasing MV concentration enhances the interfacial kinetics, it limits the transport within the electrode microstructure. The interfacial kinetics shows to be nontrivially governed by the supporting electrolyte. A surface area-permeability trade-off appears across microstructures with different electrolyte concentrations. This multiparadigm modelling workflow provides mechanistic insights between porous transport and interfacial electrochemical kinetics, enabling the coupled optimization of microstructures and electrolytes in RFBs.

title: The Greenwashing vs. Genuine Sustainability Alignment
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: The Greenwashing versus Genuine Sustainability Alignment represents a critical ethical, structural, and financial conflict within modern project governance, driven by the intense friction between corporate public relations metrics and hard
content: The Greenwashing versus Genuine Sustainability Alignment represents a critical ethical, structural, and financial conflict within modern project governance, driven by the intense friction between corporate public relations metrics and hard engineering realities. In the contemporary corporate ecosystem, projects are increasingly mandated by regulatory bodies, institutional investors, and global capital markets to achieve strict Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) compliance, carbon neutrality, and circular economy benchmarks. The core managerial dilemma arises because implementing authentic, deep-lifecycle sustainability practices requires massive upfront capital expenditure (CapEx), specialized low-carbon material procurement, prolonged environmental impact modeling, and radical transparency—investments that directly threaten the project's short-term financial profit margins and return on investment (ROI). Mechanistically, this tension drives many organizations to fall into the trap of structural greenwashing. Project planners and executive sponsors, eager to capture high ESG investment scores and satisfy public relations mandates without absorbing the corresponding financial premiums, implement superficial environmental changes. They focus on highly visible but functionally shallow adaptations—such as wrapping a building in basic solar-shading claddings or purchasing unverified carbon offsets—while maintaining a carbon-intensive, non-sustainable supply chain core. The catastrophic structural consequence manifests during the operational phase of the asset. Superficial adaptations fail to provide true lifecycle resilience against accelerating climate extremes and regulatory carbon tax adjustments. When independent auditors or investigative journalists expose the disconnect between the project's green rhetoric and its actual environmental performance, the organization faces immediate brand destruction, massive regulatory fines, and the sudden withdrawal of institutional capital. Conversely, if a project manager demands absolute adherence to genuine sustainability goals, the immediate inflation of material procurement costs and testing timelines can render the project commercially unviable within a competitive market. Resolving this deep structural conflict requires the mandatory integration of total lifecycle carbon accounting into the baseline project value definition, transforming sustainability from a cosmetic marketing overlay into a core, auditable engineering parameter.

title: Large eddy simulation and experimental investigation of liquid ammonia diffusion combustion and emissions formation under diesel-ignited JCCI conditions
summary: Under the framework of powertrain carbon neutrality, the jet-controlled compression ignition (JCCI) strategy, which utilizes diesel-ignited direct injection liquid ammonia diffusion combustion demonstrates strong potential for improving the
content: Under the framework of powertrain carbon neutrality, the jet-controlled compression ignition (JCCI) strategy, which utilizes diesel-ignited direct injection liquid ammonia diffusion combustion demonstrates strong potential for improving the power output and reducing emissions in ammonia-fueled engines. However, fundamental insights into the liquid ammonia spray processes remain insufficient, and the mechanisms governing ammonia diffusion combustion and pollutant formation require deeper examination. This study combines optical diagnostics and Large Eddy Simulation (LES) to compare diesel prior-injection and simultaneous injection strategies under dual direct‑injection conditions. The results demonstrate that for efficient combustion of the liquid ammonia spray, the ignition source should be positioned within the well-mixed region at the spray leading edge. This enables flame propagation towards the spray periphery and tail, progressively igniting the entire flammable zone and ultimately achieving complete combustion. Conversely, if ignition occurs in the spray central region, the overly lean mixture at the spray head prevents ignition, leading to substantial escape of unburned ammonia. Regarding emissions, under the diesel prior-injection condition, NO distributes throughout the spray following flame expansion, unburned ammonia is minimal, and N 2 O is primarily located at the flame periphery during the late combustion stage. In contrast, the simultaneous injection condition results in incomplete combustion, confining NO to the central region, yielding higher levels of unburned ammonia, and showing negligible N 2 O decomposition. Based on these findings, a conceptual model incorporating the “head-priority ignition” principle is proposed, correlating pollutant distribution with combustion zones to provide a theoretical basis for optimizing engine combustion and reducing emissions.

title: From brine chemistry to flowsheet: A screening framework for direct lithium extraction in geothermal and oilfield co-production settings
summary: Direct lithium extraction (DLE) from geothermal and oilfield brines is supported by many technology reviews, yet an operator holding a brine analysis still lacks a structured route to a defensible choice of technology. The review organizes
content: Direct lithium extraction (DLE) from geothermal and oilfield brines is supported by many technology reviews, yet an operator holding a brine analysis still lacks a structured route to a defensible choice of technology. The review organizes published evidence into a decision-directional screening framework mapping a co-produced brine’s chemistry, flow rate, reinjection specification and thermal integration limits onto the DLE families that remain feasible, those excluded, and the pre-treatment train implied. Chemistry windows are compiled for sorbents, ion sieves, membranes, electrochemical routes, capacitive deionization and solvent extraction, with thresholds traced to their sources and disagreements reported as ranges rather than resolved silently. Interactions that single-parameter screening misses, including silica scaling against sorbent temperature windows, naturally occurring radioactive material (NORM) accumulation on beds, and reinjection limits, are treated explicitly. Four pilot settings, the Salton Sea, the Upper Rhine Graben, Cornwall and the Smackover Formation, are reread through the framework, yielding its central pattern: every co-production project that has advanced to hardware has selected a sorption route, in three of the four an aluminium-based or proprietary sorbent operated warm to hot. A stepwise screening procedure is proposed and is then run forward, from public data only, on a project that did not shape it, E3 Lithium’s Leduc brine in Alberta; the forward reading is concordant with the route selected there and shows the grade gate to be a boundary of demonstrated practice rather than of feasibility. The procedure remains an unvalidated synthesis, and the research needed to validate it is set out.

title: Voltage support strength-constrained transmission network expansion planning for renewable-integrated grids via deep reinforcement learning
summary: Introduction The increasing penetration of inverter-based renewable energy sources (RES) presents significant challenges to power system stability by weakening grid strength, an issue often overlooked in traditional transmission network exp
content: Introduction The increasing penetration of inverter-based renewable energy sources (RES) presents significant challenges to power system stability by weakening grid strength, an issue often overlooked in traditional transmission network expansion planning (TNEP). To address this gap, this study introduces a novel planning framework that integrates data-driven uncertainty modeling with intelligent, stability-aware decision-making. Methods We employ an improved Neural Koopman algorithm combined with the K-Means method to extract representative operational scenarios and formulate the TNEP problem as a Markov Decision Process (MDP). A Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) agent, specifically a Double Deep Q-Network (DDQN), is then trained to determine an optimal, sequential construction strategy. Crucially, the dynamic Short-Circuit Ratio (SCR) is incorporated as a penalty term within the agent’s reward function and enforced through an exact post hoc feasibility check to proactively ensure system stability. Results Validated on the high-renewable penetration standard system CEPRI-VC-88, the proposed framework yielded a plan that successfully reduced annual wind curtailment from 12.8% to 1.5% and completely eliminated scenarios with inadequate SCR at a moderate investment cost. Discussion The results demonstrate that this DRL-based approach provides a powerful and forward-looking paradigm for TNEP, effectively balancing economic, renewable accommodation, and dynamic stability objectives to foster a more resilient power grid.

title: BIM4SM Building Envelope Performance Dashboard
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Interactive HTML dashboard for the BIM4SM (Building Information Modelling for Sustainable Maintenance) framework, developed to support real-time monitoring, sensitivity-based retrofit prioritisation, and lifecycle scenario comparison for bu
content: Interactive HTML dashboard for the BIM4SM (Building Information Modelling for Sustainable Maintenance) framework, developed to support real-time monitoring, sensitivity-based retrofit prioritisation, and lifecycle scenario comparison for building envelope performance. Validated on a naturally ventilated institutional hostel case study at IIT Gandhinagar, India. Displays key performance indicators (EUI, CDH, carbon intensity, peak temperature), an age-based sensitivity ranking, a 27-scenario envelope comparison, and standards-linked retrofit recommendations.

title: MOVPE growth and characterization of AlPN layers for HFETs
source: Strathprints: The University of Strathclyde institutional repository (University of Strathclyde)
summary: The growth of AlPN layers by metalorganic vapor phase epitaxy (MOVPE) and their use as barrier layers on GaN buffer layers for heterojunction field effect transistors (HFETs) was investigated. Quantitative energy-dispersive X-ray spectrosco
content: The growth of AlPN layers by metalorganic vapor phase epitaxy (MOVPE) and their use as barrier layers on GaN buffer layers for heterojunction field effect transistors (HFETs) was investigated. Quantitative energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX), wavelength-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (WDX), and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) measurements were used to determine the atomic P content of the AlPN layers. PH3 and tertiarybutyl phosphine (tBP) proved to be very similar P precursors for the MOVPE growth of AlPN layers. The AlPN HFET epitaxial layer structures were characterized by atomic force microscopy (AFM), X-ray diffraction (XRD), Hall effect, conductivity, and capacitance–voltage (CV) measurements. AlPN/AlN/GaN/sapphire HFET devices were fabricated and characterized. The results indicate that AlPN, similar to Ga1-xPxN, suffers from a preferential incorporation of P onto the group III lattice site instead of the desired N site, and may therefore not allow for downscaling of HFET devices as predicted for the lattice changes when incorporating P at N sites.

title: FRAMEWORK DEVELOPMENT OF BIOPHILIC MODEL FOR CORPORATE BUILDINGS
source: TPM Testing, psychometrics, methodology in applied psychology
summary: Environmental degradation and unorganized cities are rising issues because of a growing population in an era of fast globalization. People confronted a dilemma with denser and congested urban development, which highlighted the fragility of
content: Environmental degradation and unorganized cities are rising issues because of a growing population in an era of fast globalization. People confronted a dilemma with denser and congested urban development, which highlighted the fragility of towns and their residents. There are no such rules that govern the general equilibrium of the ecosystem due to rising urbanization and unplanned cities. As a result, global temperatures will rise by 1.5 degrees Celsius by 2050. Rapid building has made a substantial impact on the natural world to meet the requirements of a rising population. It contributes to global warming by generating more than 30% of the world's emissions of greenhouse gases. Buildings are the largest energy consumers and equivalent to approximately 40% of all substantial energy sources for example nuclear energy, hydropower, and fossil fuels. Sustainable construction and development methods are being used to reduce negative consequences and create an environment that is more environmentally friendly. Applying biophilic design concepts in building construction to generate connections between individuals and the environment is one method of achieving sustainability. The various categories of biophilic design are identified, evaluated, and their key components discussed in this study's thorough literature research. Next, using building evaluation methods, we examine the advantages of biophilic design in attaining sustainability, including improved health, wellness, work efficiency, and revenue generation. The results help in developing a biophilic model framework that can be used by designers and architectures for a more sustainable, healthy and resilient environment in the corporate sector. In addition, by indicating the framework, knowledge gaps are discovered to spur further investigation and practical examination of biophilic design approaches.

title: A global base temperature dataset for residential building energy demand modelling
summary: Abstract. Accurate building energy demand modeling is critical to decarbonizing regional energy systems. The cooling and heating degree-day models are widely used due to their simplicity and low data requirements; however, the lack of accur
content: Abstract. Accurate building energy demand modeling is critical to decarbonizing regional energy systems. The cooling and heating degree-day models are widely used due to their simplicity and low data requirements; however, the lack of accurate base temperature data limits their performance. In particular, the scarcity of high temporal resolution building energy demand data constrains regional-scale base temperature estimation through conventional methods such as the energy signature method and the performance line method. To address this limitation, this study develops a global regional-scale base temperature dataset based on the BiLSTM neural network framework with an attention mechanism. The dataset includes both cooling base temperature (Tcool) and heating base temperature (Theat) for each region, defined at a spatial scale equivalent to a U.S. state or a Chinese province. The BiLSTM framework demonstrates strong performance, with RMSE values of 1.39°C for training and 1.33°C for testing, and Pearson correlation coefficients of 0.84 for Tcool and 0.70 for Theat. Predicted results show that global Tcool ranges from 19–25°C and Theat from 14–18°C, consistent with physical principles. External validations using 16 independent datasets demonstrate that the predicted base temperatures significantly improve the accuracy of building energy demand modeling, reducing RMSE by 10.01% for cooling and 10.02% for heating, compared to official or empirical base temperatures. This dataset supplements sparse observational base temperature data and enhances the accuracy of building energy demand modeling, contributing to low-carbon energy system planning, broader climate impact assessment and weather-related financial applications. The proposed global Tbase dataset can be acquired from https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.30646376.v2 (He et al., 2025).

title: Light absorption properties and composition of water-soluble brown carbon in North China Plain: implication for an enhancing role of nitrogenous organic compounds
summary: Abstract. Brown carbon (BrC), an efficiently light-absorbing carbonaceous aerosol, exerts significant impacts on the global energy budget and regional climate, attracting growing scientific attention. To advance understanding of the spatial
content: Abstract. Brown carbon (BrC), an efficiently light-absorbing carbonaceous aerosol, exerts significant impacts on the global energy budget and regional climate, attracting growing scientific attention. To advance understanding of the spatial variability of atmospheric BrC and its dominant formation pathways in the North China Plain (NCP), light absorption properties, chemical composition and formation process of the water-soluble BrC in 2023 winter were investigated by conducting simultaneous measurements at five sites across the NCP, namely, Beijing, Tianjin, Luancheng (rural site), Handan and Jinan. Our results showed that the average light absorption coefficient at 365 nm (abs365) in Luancheng was approximately 1.1–3.5 times higher than those in urban ones; While mass absorption efficiency displayed a distinctly different spatial pattern, with the strongest light-absorptivity (1.40 ± 0.02 m2 g−1) recorded in Jinan. Notably, average abs365 in four urban sites exhibited a decline of ~ 45 % from 2018 to 2023 compared to those previous observations. Furthermore, the light-absorptivity of BrC was enhanced from clean to haze period at the most sampling sites along with the increasing N:C ratio, indicating that nitrogenous organic compounds (NOCs) were the important BrC chromophores in the NCP. Additionally, more than 50 % of NOCs were confirmed to be secondarily formed; and the ammonia-driven aqueous reactions were identified as the predominant pathway governing the secondary formation of these NOCs. These results elucidate the substantial contribution of NOCs to atmospheric BrC in the NCP, and further confirm the importance of ammonia emission for alleviating haze and BrC pollution in this region.

title: Drought responses of a Norway spruce forest on drained peat soil: combining sap-flow sensors, eddy-covariance, meteorological, soil and UAV data
summary: Abstract. The summer of 2021 brought a severe drought to southern Finland. We explored how a drained boreal peatland forest responds to drought by combining a wide range of in situ monitoring and Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) remote sensing
content: Abstract. The summer of 2021 brought a severe drought to southern Finland. We explored how a drained boreal peatland forest responds to drought by combining a wide range of in situ monitoring and Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) remote sensing. A dataset combining eddy-covariance (EC) fluxes, sap-flow sensors, UAV mapping, soil and weather data was collected. Spruce stand reaction to drought is examined at sub-daily to seasonal time scales, and its temporal and spatial features are identified separately for a recently thinned Continuous Cover Forestry (CCF) block and a control block. Sap flow data showed that the CCF-harvested block shows greater tree resilience to high vapour pressure deficit (VPD) than the control block, likely due to the higher soil water availability during the rainless and hot period. At the same time, both the control and CCF harvest blocks had notably reduced net ecosystem exchange (NEE) and increased Bowen ratio, particularly on high VPD days. The UAV surveys indicated that trees in the CCF block tend to have higher canopy temperatures and lower Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) than in the control block, implying their possible susceptibility to more extreme drought.

title: Modular Cyano-fluoroalkylation of Unactivated Alkenes Enabled by Photoinduced Fe-LMCT Catalysis
summary: Abstract We describe the implementation of an iron catalyzed cyano-fluoroalkylation of unactivated alkenes that leverages inexpensive trifluoroacetic acid (CF3CO2H) and related carboxylic acids (CFnRCO2H) as radical fluoroalkyl sources, tog
content: Abstract We describe the implementation of an iron catalyzed cyano-fluoroalkylation of unactivated alkenes that leverages inexpensive trifluoroacetic acid (CF3CO2H) and related carboxylic acids (CFnRCO2H) as radical fluoroalkyl sources, together with tosyl cyanide (TsCN) as a low-toxicity cyanation reagent. Notably, the mild and redox-neutral conditions of the method are compatible with a broad range of substrates, including alkenes containing biologically relevant motifs (40 examples, up to 83% yield). The resulting β-fluoroalkylated nitriles can be diversely derivatized to afford other valuable fluorinated sp3-rich architectures. Mechanistic studies have revealed the key role of a protonated bipyridine-based ligand in enhancing reaction efficiency.

title: How Strategic Leaders Drive Firms in Ecosystems: Envisioning Value, Orchestrating Knowledge, and Shifting Roles
summary: Abstract Research on business ecosystems has illuminated how ecosystems emerge, evolve, and transform, revealing ecosystem‐level dynamics and the central actors that orchestrate them. Yet, it is individual firms that continuously attempt to
content: Abstract Research on business ecosystems has illuminated how ecosystems emerge, evolve, and transform, revealing ecosystem‐level dynamics and the central actors that orchestrate them. Yet, it is individual firms that continuously attempt to establish and shift the roles they play within ecosystems through the vision and choices of their strategic leaders. How do strategic leaders drive these shifts? Through a longitudinal case study of Dallara Automobili (1972–2025), we trace how the CEO's prior professional experience shaped an evolving theory of value – a set of conjectures about how value should be created that guided the development of organizational routines enabling progressively more expansive knowledge orchestration. This process shifted Dallara from a peripheral component supplier to a boundary‐spanning knowledge orchestrator. Our recursive process model theorizes how the leader's conjectures drive firm role shifts within an ecosystem: experience shapes the leader's theory of value, which drives organizational routines and knowledge orchestration; knowledge orchestration, in turn, redefines the firm's ecosystem role. Ecosystem responses then feed back, augmenting prior experience and, in turn, refining the theory of value so that each round operates at a broader scope. We contribute to ecosystem research by identifying knowledge orchestration as the mechanism through which a leader's theory of value translates into shifts in the firm's role and by showing how this process unfolds recursively as ecosystem responses reshape the leader's conjectures.

title: JWST Reveals the Kuiper Belt–like Compositions of the Uranian Rings and Small Moons
summary: Abstract We present the JWST NIRSpec 1–5 μ m spectra of the Uranian rings and four ring moons: Puck, Perdita, Portia, and Juliet. We find that the compositions of the rings and moons strongly resemble water-type Kuiper Belt objects, showing
content: Abstract We present the JWST NIRSpec 1–5 μ m spectra of the Uranian rings and four ring moons: Puck, Perdita, Portia, and Juliet. We find that the compositions of the rings and moons strongly resemble water-type Kuiper Belt objects, showing deep 3.0 μ m O–H and water-ice features as well as the CO 2 band at 4.27 μ m. The volatiles show a radial trend of decreasing volatile abundance at closer radial distance to the planet, consistent with recent estimates of the densities of the innermost moons. Given the observed compositional signatures, we suggest two ways to reconcile the history of the small inner moons with that of the regular ones. The first is that the Uranus-tilting collision produced a disk from an impactor formed out of material similar to that which comprises water-rich Kuiper Belt objects, and the ring moons are small undifferentiated remnants of that process. Alternatively, the rings and ring moons postdate the formation of the regular moons, and formed from the later tidal disruption of a several-hundred-kilometer-sized, undifferentiated, water-type Kuiper Belt object.

title: ZIF-8 Nanoparticles: Zinc Ion Release, In Vitro Biocompatibility, and Evaluation in Galleria mellonella
summary: Abstract Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), and Zeolitic Imidazolate Framework-8 (ZIF-8) in particular, have found wide application in the therapeutic field. Their structure, size, and porosity can be tuned, and they can be synthesized using
content: Abstract Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), and Zeolitic Imidazolate Framework-8 (ZIF-8) in particular, have found wide application in the therapeutic field. Their structure, size, and porosity can be tuned, and they can be synthesized using various methods. However, their biocompatibility and potential cytotoxicity remain insufficiently investigated. In this study, ZIF-8 nanoparticles were synthesized at room temperature using a rapid method with methanol as the solvent and characterized in terms of their chemical composition, structural properties, ion release behavior, and biocompatibility. The Zn ion release profile of ZIF-8 particles into Tris-HCl buffer medium was obtained through inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES) under dynamic flow conditions, indicating a gradual and continuous release over 48 h. According to in vitro assays, MC3T3-E1 mouse preosteoblast cells maintained high viability at concentrations up to 100 μg·mL–1, while direct exposure of VH10 human fibroblast cells to 100 μg·mL–1 ZIF-8 reduced metabolic activity without significant membrane damage. However, no evident toxicity was observed in the eluate-based assay at this concentration. The findings were supported by the outcomes from the static ion release studies in DMEM cell culture medium, where ICP-OES showed that the level of Zn cations was lower than 9.5 μg·mL–1 in 100 μg·mL–1 ZIF-8 samples. The DNA fragmentation assay also indicated no detectable fragmentation at 100 μg·mL–1, suggesting the absence of apoptotic DNA damage in MC3T3-E1 cells under indirect exposure conditions. In addition, ZIF-8 was evaluated in vivo using the Galleria mellonella larval model, and samples up to 100 μg·mL–1 showed 100% survival and only minor reductions in health index score. The study underscores the importance of selecting appropriate methods for biocompatibility assessment, while also demonstrating the cytocompatibility of the investigated ZIF-8 nanoparticles, which may be associated with the relatively low measured Zn ion release.

title: Rethinking municipal electricity in South Africa: Rooftop solar PV, revenue and just energy transitions in the City of Johannesburg
source: Journal of Energy in Southern Africa
summary: South Africa’s deepening electricity crisis, marked by persistent load-shedding and escalating tariffs, has accelerated private solar photovoltaic (PV) installations. This rapid transition has raised concerns about municipal revenue erosion
content: South Africa’s deepening electricity crisis, marked by persistent load-shedding and escalating tariffs, has accelerated private solar photovoltaic (PV) installations. This rapid transition has raised concerns about municipal revenue erosion, cross-subsidisation and energy inequality. The City of Johannesburg Metropolitan Municipality (CoJ) is at the centre of this transition, and is grappling with the implications for its business model and how private solar PV can be leveraged to support a just energy transition. This paper is written from the perspective of City officials, and examines the extent of rooftop solar PV and its impact on municipal revenue, finances and grid management. The paper draws on municipal records, internal meetings and reports, and an industry dataset. The analysis reveals that official records substantially underrepresent solar PV installations in the CoJ. Despite the concern that private solar PV erodes revenue, this analysis highlights that technical losses, load-shedding, and customer non-payment have a far greater financial impact. This paper challenges the assumption that distributed power undermines social justice, and rather points to the need for tariff reform, away from volumetric sales towards fixed network charges, to stabilise municipal finances. Rather than framing distributed solar PV as inherently threatening to municipal revenue and social justice, the paper shows that these outcomes depend on how municipal business models, tariffs and governance adapt to and leverage off decentralised energy.

title: Self-Catalyzed Hastelloy Fiber Paper (HAP) Porous Transport Layer for Oxygen Evolution Reaction in Anion Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis
summary: Abstract Hastelloy fiber paper (HAP) can be used as the oxygen evolution reaction porous transport layer (PTL) without using a catalyst layer in anion exchange membrane water electrolysis. It is combined with Ru on nickel fiber paper (NFP)
content: Abstract Hastelloy fiber paper (HAP) can be used as the oxygen evolution reaction porous transport layer (PTL) without using a catalyst layer in anion exchange membrane water electrolysis. It is combined with Ru on nickel fiber paper (NFP) (hydrogen evolution reaction PTL) to form an asymmetric Ru/NFP(−)//HAP(+) single-cell system. The experimental results for electrodeposited Co(OH)2 on HAP are also demonstrated for comparison. At 70 °C, the cell delivers 725.67 mA cm–2 at 1.8 V under cathode-wet conditions and maintains 701.34 mA cm–2 under cathode-dry operation. A 5000-cycle accelerated stress test (AST) confirms the good operational stability of the system under dynamic cycling conditions. In addition, the effect of Co(OH)2 electrodeposition on the HAP anode was further investigated to show the current density decreases to 485.59 mA cm–2 at 1.8 V when operated at 70 °C. The AST stability also degrades with Co(OH)2 deposition. Further analysis indicates that the electrodeposited Co(OH)2 coating may alter the pore structure and surface wettability of the catalyst layer, leading to mass-transport limitations at high current densities, including hindered ion transport and inefficient oxygen bubble removal.

title: Rice Straw-Derived Cellulose Nanocrystal-based Adsorptive Filtration Nanocomposite Membranes for Efficient Removal of Methylene Blue
source: Innovation of Chemistry & Materials for Sustainability
summary: Industrial wastewater, particularly from textile, paper, and dye industries, often contains methylene blue (MB), a hazardous synthetic dye and causes health hazards. Cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs), especially when modified with polydopamine
content: Industrial wastewater, particularly from textile, paper, and dye industries, often contains methylene blue (MB), a hazardous synthetic dye and causes health hazards. Cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs), especially when modified with polydopamine (PDA), offer a sustainable and efficient adsorbent due to their high surface area, abundant functional groups, and natural availability. Furthermore, their ordered self-assembled structure can create a porous and tortuous path in the composite membranes, desirable for efficient filtration. Herein, PDA-modified rice straw-derived cellulose nanocrystals (RSDCNCs)-based biocompatible adsorption filtration nanocomposite membranes were fabricated to efficiently remove MB dye from water. A certain feed ratio of polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) as a binder and glutaraldehyde (GA) as a crosslinker were added with RSDCNC and the mixture was deposited onto a Whatman filter paper substrate via vacuum filtration to fabricate the adsorptive membranes. The addition of a binder and a crosslinker in a requisite ratio enhanced the flexibility and strength of the membranes and provided mechanical stability against filtration. The as-prepared adsorptive filtration membranes having an optimized adsorbent area density of 1.44 mg.cm-² have demonstrated higher removal efficiency, repeatability, and reusability for the treatment of MB contaminated water. Reusability analysis using 20 mL of initial 10 ppm dye solution showed that the PVA/RSDCNC-50-50 membrane displayed the highest removal efficiency up to the 5th cycle of filtration. The removal efficiency of 99.6, 99.3, 98.3, 97.7, and 89.0% were obtained after 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, and 5th filtration cycle, respectively, with MB removal time 8-15 min per filtration cycle. Furthermore, the optimized PVA/RSDCNC-50-50 membranes exhibited an MB dye removal efficiency of approximately 94% at 50 ppm and 69% at 100 ppm initial dye concentrations. The catechol groups, imine and amine functionality, and aromatic moieties of PDA, porous morphology of the modified substrate, and abundant surface hydroxyl groups and the tortuosity created by CNCs in the membrane are responsible factors for the efficient dye removal. Therefore, all these features and properties make the bio-based PVA/RSDCNC adsorptive filtration membrane a potential material for diversified dye contaminated wastewater remediation, heavy metal ions, and oil-water separation.

title: Drought memory and vegetation shifts triggered by recurrent extreme drought events in alpine peatlands amplify the sensitivity of carbon sink function to drought
summary: Climate change is expected to intensify the frequency and severity of extreme drought events, profoundly influencing terrestrial ecosystem carbon budgets. Peatlands are crucial carbon reservoirs in the global carbon cycle, storing nearly on
content: Climate change is expected to intensify the frequency and severity of extreme drought events, profoundly influencing terrestrial ecosystem carbon budgets. Peatlands are crucial carbon reservoirs in the global carbon cycle, storing nearly one-third of the world's soil carbon. However, our understanding of how alpine peatland ecosystems respond to recurrent extreme droughts, particularly in terms of carbon flux dynamics, remains incomplete. Through a six-year in situ experiment, we investigated the effects of sustained extreme drought on carbon flux dynamics in alpine peatlands. Our results demonstrate that extreme drought significantly reduces net ecosystem exchange (NEE), gross ecosystem productivity (GEP), and ecosystem respiration (Reco). These impacts intensified with cumulative drought years due to weakened CO 2 sink resistance. Moreover, extreme drought disrupts the stability of the peatland's CO 2 absorption capacity, with CO 2 and CH 4 fluxes being more sensitive to soil moisture than to temperature. However, as arid conditions intensify, the influence of drought-induced soil moisture alterations on peatland carbon sinks wanes. Notably, temperature exhibits significant negative correlations with the resistance of NEE ( R = −0.530, P < 0.05) and Reco ( R = −0.473, P < 0.05), key indicators defined as the ecosystem's capacity to maintain stable carbon exchange rates despite the perturbations caused by extreme drought. After six years of extreme drought, we observed a shift in plant community composition, with a decline in hygrophyte proportions and an increase in xerophyte species and abundance. NEE demonstrated a unimodal relationship with aboveground biomass, peaking at 450 g/m 2 , while GEP exhibited an inverse pattern. These findings emphasize the importance of integrating plant community dynamics and drought memory effects into Earth system models to enhance predictions of extreme drought impacts on peatland carbon sink functionality under future climate scenarios, thereby amplifying understanding the sensitivity of these ecosystems to drought.

title: Matcha (Japanese ground green tea) and cognitive function
summary: Abstract Matcha is a finely ground powder made from shade-grown green tea leaves. It is primarily produced in Japan. Drinking matcha tea results in higher intake of green tea bioactives than drinking other types of green tea. Studies have f
content: Abstract Matcha is a finely ground powder made from shade-grown green tea leaves. It is primarily produced in Japan. Drinking matcha tea results in higher intake of green tea bioactives than drinking other types of green tea. Studies have found that matcha consumption may enhance cognitive function in situations with and without psychological stress, in the short and long term, and in different age groups. The effects of matcha on cognitive function may be due to stress reduction, improved sleep quality, an increased supply of vitamin K, altered intestinal microbiota composition, decreased oxidative stress, enhanced cholinergic brain function, and increased cortical capillary network angiogenesis. Matcha’s stress-reducing efficiency appears to be influenced by differences in the quantities and ratios of its components, which may affect cognitive function. Matcha must contain high levels of theanine to have beneficial effects on stress and anxiety. Furthermore, the ratio of epigallocatechin gallate and caffeine to theanine and arginine must be low. Since not all marketed matcha products worldwide meet these conditions, quality control is important. Harnessing matcha’s beneficial properties may effectively support cognitive function and prevent cognitive decline and dementia.

title: Assessing mangrove sensitivity to thermal variations through a satellite-based analysis on the southern São Paulo coast, Brazil
summary: Abstract Mangroves near subtropical range limits may benefit from fewer cold constraints, yet warmer conditions can also increase atmospheric water demand. These competing possibilities were examined in the Cananéia-Iguape Coastal System, s
content: Abstract Mangroves near subtropical range limits may benefit from fewer cold constraints, yet warmer conditions can also increase atmospheric water demand. These competing possibilities were examined in the Cananéia-Iguape Coastal System, southeastern Brazil, by combining ERA5 2 m air temperature with MODIS normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI), enhanced vegetation index (EVI), and leaf area index (LAI). Air-temperature trends were assessed for 1979–2019 with the Mann-Kendall test and Sen’s slope. Temperature-vegetation associations were calculated for 2003–2019 from mangrove-wide means and from individual grid cells at annual, monthly, and fixed calendar-quarter scales. Mean annual air temperature increased by about 0.02 °C year⁻ 1 ; the highest quarter-scale rate occurred in July–September (0.03 °C year⁻ 1 ). Annual temperature correlated positively with NDVI ( r = 0.61, R 2 = 0.38, p = 0.009) and EVI ( r = 0.55, R 2 = 0.30, p = 0.022), whereas the LAI relationship was not significant ( r = 0.27, R 2 = 0.07, p = 0.304). The sign of the association changed within the year: NDVI and EVI were negative in July–September, while positive EVI and LAI relationships occurred in October-December. Significant grid-cell relationships occupied limited and discontinuous areas. The temperature record shows regional warming, whereas canopy associations vary among metrics, periods, and locations. Given the bivariate design and coarse ERA5 grid, these associations should not be interpreted as causal or as responses to temperature alone.

title: Ultrathin Li 1.3 Al 0.3 Ti 1.7 (PO 4 ) 3 -Based Flexible Solid Electrolyte for All-Solid-State Lithium Batteries
summary: Abstract NASICON-type solid electrolytes are highly attractive for solid-state lithium batteries due to their superior ionic conductivity and low cost. However, practical implementation remains severely limited by their inherent brittleness
content: Abstract NASICON-type solid electrolytes are highly attractive for solid-state lithium batteries due to their superior ionic conductivity and low cost. However, practical implementation remains severely limited by their inherent brittleness, poor solid-solid contact, and severe side reactions with lithium metal. Herein, we report a flexible Li 1.3 Al 0.3 Ti 1.7 (PO 4 ) 3 (LATP)-based composite solid electrolyte film fabricated via an in-situ polymerization strategy. This film achieves an exceptionally high LATP loading of 90 wt% within a minimal thickness of 20 μm, ensuring outstanding thermal stability and safety. Crucially, the composite electrolyte delivers a competitive roomtemperature ionic conductivity of 1.5 × 10 -4 S cm -1 and an expansive electrochemical window exceeding 5.1 V. Consequently, symmetric Li||Li cells demonstrate excellent interfacial stability, sustaining over 600 hours of steady cycling at 60 °C and 0.1 mA cm -2 . Furthermore, full cells paired with LFP and NCM811 cathodes display superior long-term cyclability and rate performance.

title: Manganese-modified biochar enhances white-rot fungi-mediated lignocellulose humification: insights from molecular transformation and multi-omics analyses
summary: Humic substance formation is essential for soil health, yet natural humification is slow, and synthetic production is often inefficient. White-rot fungi (WRF)-mediated lignocellulose humification shows potential but is limited by slow subst
content: Humic substance formation is essential for soil health, yet natural humification is slow, and synthetic production is often inefficient. White-rot fungi (WRF)-mediated lignocellulose humification shows potential but is limited by slow substrate degradation. Given the high biocatalytic potential of Mn(II) and its compatibility with the enzyme system of WRF, manganese-modified biochar (MBC) was utilized to enhance the degradation and conversion efficiency of lignocellulose. A 35-day solid-state fermentation experiment showed that 5% MBC addition increased lignin degradation by 93.4%, humic acid content by 47.7%, and polymerization degree by 112.4% compared with CK. Mechanistically, first, MBC enhanced extracellular lignocellulose-degrading enzymes and Mn-associated Fenton-like oxidation, thereby improving lignocellulose depolymerization. Second, interpretable machine learning and mass difference-based association analysis identified key molecular reactivity traits, suggesting that MBC facilitated humification by promoting the selective generation and conversion of reactive precursor molecules. In particular, enhanced DOM reactivity and increased precursor formation through deamination, dealkylation, and delignification were associated with the generation of more aromatic, oxygen-functionalized, and unsaturated humic-like substances, likely through polyphenol-dominated pathways. Finally, transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses indicated that MBC upregulated the expression of CAZyme-related genes and metabolic pathways associated with precursor generation, including phenolic/quinone biosynthesis, indicating that enhanced substrate depolymerization and subsequent precursor transformation jointly contributed to lignocellulose humification. Overall, this study provides mechanistic insights into how MBC enhances WRF-mediated lignocellulose humification and offers a theoretical basis for optimizing the bioconversion of lignocellulose-rich organic wastes.

title: Recognition and mechanism of M. tuberculosis cell wall galactan transport
summary: Mycobacterial-derived lipid-linked galactan (LLG) is an essential component of the Mycobacterial tuberculosis (Mtb) cell wall core arabinogalactan (AG), a well-established virulence factor and target of anti-tubercular drugs. Cross-membrane
content: Mycobacterial-derived lipid-linked galactan (LLG) is an essential component of the Mycobacterial tuberculosis (Mtb) cell wall core arabinogalactan (AG), a well-established virulence factor and target of anti-tubercular drugs. Cross-membrane translocation of LLG is energetically unfavorable and is therefore catalyzed by WzmWzt, a prominent member of the polysaccharide ABC transporter sub-family. Here we present cryo-EM structures of WzmWztMtb to uncover critical steps of Mtb LLG translocation. Notably, densities suggestive of the mycobacterial-derived LLG substrates were observed in the structure of WzmWztMtb, indicating that the substrate may bind through two Wzm and two Wzt subunits. This proposed LLG binding is fulfilled by a fully upward extension of the Wzt gate helix, which serves as a critical step to prime Wzt for dimerization. The ATP-bound structure revealed a remarkable downward movement of the gate helix, together with the Wzt dimerization. The third, DDM/ATP-bound structure captured WztWzmMtb in an intermediate state with two DDM molecules in the Wzm central cavity. Using two conditional mycobacterial mutants for functional analyses, we have identified residues on the Wzm N-terminal interface helix (IFN) and on the Wzt helical domain are essential for LLG recognition and translocation in vivo. These data provide a clear structural basis for the development of Mtb cell wall targeted therapeutics for global tuberculosis treatment. In this work, Wei and colleagues reveal how an essential Mycobacterium tuberculosis transporter recognizes and translocates a cell-wall galactan chain across the membrane, providing a structural framework for developing tuberculosis drugs.

title: Voltammetric studies of TiO2-nanographite based composites
summary: Titanium dioxide (TiO 2 ) is a promising electrode material for use as an electrode in electrochemical energy storage. However, its low electrical conductivity limits its performance. This study investigated the influence of nanographite in
content: Titanium dioxide (TiO 2 ) is a promising electrode material for use as an electrode in electrochemical energy storage. However, its low electrical conductivity limits its performance. This study investigated the influence of nanographite incorporation and ionic liquid (IL) addition on the structural and electrochemical properties of TiO 2 . Hydrothermally synthesized TiO 2 nanoparticles and TiO 2 modified with the ILs triethylammonium-propane-sulfonic acid tetrafluoroborate ([TEA-PS][BF 4 ]) (TB) and 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium hydrogen sulfate ([BMIM][HSO 4 ]) (BM) were used to prepare thick-film electrodes of pure TiO 2 (T) and TiO 2 /nanographite (T/NG) composites. Diffractograms revealed TiO 2 oxide phases in the anatase form, along with characteristic graphite peaks. Scanning electron microscopy revealed porous films composed of agglomerated TiO 2 , while Raman spectroscopy confirmed the integrity of the graphitic framework through the characteristic D, G, and 2D bands. Cyclic voltammetry showed that the incorporation of nanographite increased the voltammetric charge by up to three orders of magnitude compared with pure TiO 2 . After normalization by the active mass, the T/NG/BM electrode exhibited the highest specific charge, reaching 6.93 C g −1 under cathodic polarization, whereas pure TiO 2 remained below 0.22 C g −1 . The distinct electrochemical responses obtained for the two ionic liquids indicate that they modify the interfacial charge-storage mechanism through different kinetic pathways. Overall, the results support a hybrid charge-storage mechanism involving surface-confined Faradaic reactions coupled with pseudocapacitive contributions at the TiO 2 /nanographite interface.

title: Forest management, climate change, and roe deer: A conceptual model of how silvicultural systems shape habitat, population density, and browsing impacts
summary: Management of roe deer in European forests may be challenging due to their impact on tree regeneration and potential negative effects on tree species composition, forest resilience and various ecosystem services including timber production.
content: Management of roe deer in European forests may be challenging due to their impact on tree regeneration and potential negative effects on tree species composition, forest resilience and various ecosystem services including timber production. However, silvicultural practices themselves are key drivers in shaping roe deer habitat and consequently affecting deer population densities and the browsing susceptibility of young trees. Silvicultural interventions shape forest structures such as canopy closure, and thus the light availability and thermal cover at the forest floor. Light availability on the forest floor in turn determines vegetation growth and therefore forage availability and quality, as well as hiding opportunities for roe deer. Additionally, natural disturbances such as bark beetle outbreaks increasingly affect European forests at different spatial scales, influencing the interactions between roe deer and forests, while also underscoring the need for increased forest resilience amid climate change. This review provides an overview of the observed and potential impacts of silviculture and climate change–related disturbances on deer population density and browsing. It systematically assesses the effects of these disturbances on habitat conditions, offers a framework for managers to anticipate potential conflicts, and highlights key research needs for the future. We developed a conceptual model for the dynamics of roe deer populations, habitat use, silvicultural systems and forest structure as well as disturbances under climate change and evaluated the available literature. We expected that different silvicultural systems result in distinctive spatial and temporal patterns in resources and cover, and consequently roe deer densities and browsing susceptibility of young trees. However, the literature review revealed a substantial research gap, as very few studies assessed the impact of various silvicultural practices on roe deer directly. Empirical comparisons of management practices face many methodological challenges, and solid evidence is vital for promoting resilient forest practices — especially as disturbances are linked to climate change phenomena with potentially significant consequences on deer dynamics and browsing patterns.

title: The safety case for a deep geological repository in Switzerland: radiological consequence analysis and study of the barrier efficiency
summary: Geological repositories for radioactive waste are sited and designed to provide a set of natural and engineered barriers that isolate the waste from the human environment and contain its associated radionuclides. Nonetheless, some release o
content: Geological repositories for radioactive waste are sited and designed to provide a set of natural and engineered barriers that isolate the waste from the human environment and contain its associated radionuclides. Nonetheless, some release of radionuclides from a geological repository cannot be excluded over the Time frame of hundreds of thousands of years during which the waste presents a potential hazard. Thus, radiological consequence analysis is a key element of the post-closure safety case for deep geological repositories and provides essential insight into the efficiency of the multi-barrier system. This paper presents the current methodology and selected results of the radiological consequence analysis for a combined repository for high-level waste and low- and intermediate-level waste in an Opalinus Clay rock formation hundreds of metres below ground at a proposed site in Northern Switzerland. Deterministic and probabilistic simulations are performed to evaluate radionuclide transport, barrier efficiency, and associated uncertainties. Radionuclide migration in the liquid phase is modelled for a wide range of potentially safety-relevant radionuclides, while gas-phase transport focuses on C-14 released as methane under two-phase flow conditions. Results show that calculated dose rates are several orders of magnitude below Swiss regulatory protection criterion, demonstrating a large safety margin. Long-lived, weakly sorbing radionuclides, particularly I-129, dominate the calculated dose in a reference safety scenario that corresponds to the expected evolution of the repository and in a range of other scenarios, while most other radionuclides are effectively retained within the engineered barriers and the Opalinus Clay host rock. Probabilistic analyses and sensitivity studies identify key parameters controlling radionuclide release. Overall, the analysis confirms the robustness of the multi-barrier system and provides improved understanding of the Swiss deep geological repository system.

title: Research on Current Fixed-Point Excitation Detection Method for Internal Defects in Prebaked Anode Carbon Blocks
summary: Internal defects such as cracks and pores in prebaked anodes severely affect aluminum electrolysis efficiency and energy consumption. Existing detection methods face an irreconcilable contradiction among speed, cost, and accuracy. To addres
content: Internal defects such as cracks and pores in prebaked anodes severely affect aluminum electrolysis efficiency and energy consumption. Existing detection methods face an irreconcilable contradiction among speed, cost, and accuracy. To address this issue, this paper proposes a current fixed-point excitation detection technique, which inverses local resistivity anomalies through multi-point potential difference measurements, enabling rapid identification of internal defects in anodes. In this study, a numerical model of electrical conduction in prebaked anodes is established using COMSOL Multiphysics 6.2 to systematically analyze the influence of defect geometric dimensions on the surface potential difference distribution. The effectiveness of the method is verified through validation experiments on anodes with prefabricated defects. The results show that defect width has the most significant effect on potential difference; when the width increases from 100 mm to 300 mm, the sheet resistivity of the defect region rises from 50.95 μΩ·m to 125.1 μΩ·m. Under dual-defect conditions, the inter-defect sheet potential difference is lower than the defect-free baseline, exhibiting a “valley” characteristic. The relative error between experimental and simulated potential differences in the middle region of the anode ranges from 3.24% to 9.28%, and significant potential difference peaks appear in all defective sheets. This method provides a feasible technical approach and laboratory-based validation foundation for the online nondestructive testing of internal defects in prebaked anodes, and clearly delineates the developmental stage of the present study.

title: Photoluminescent Color Centers on a Mainstream Silicon Photonic Foundry Platform
summary: ABSTRACT Silicon photonic integrated circuits fabricated on commercial CMOS‐compatible foundries have propelled major advances in data center communication, quantum computing, and artificial intelligence due to their scalability, mass produ
content: ABSTRACT Silicon photonic integrated circuits fabricated on commercial CMOS‐compatible foundries have propelled major advances in data center communication, quantum computing, and artificial intelligence due to their scalability, mass production, low cost, and high performance. However, the indirect bandgap of silicon prevents the realization of efficient silicon light sources on these mainstream silicon‐on‐insulator (SOI) platforms. Luminescent color centers in silicon have emerged as a promising approach to fabricate monolithic light sources from the same foundry SOI. Despite the potential, all prior work relies heavily on custom, non‐foundry‐compatible fabrication and Front‐End‐Of‐Line (FEOL) processes, due to challenges in creating color centers in commercial CMOS‐compatible foundries. In this work, we demonstrate W‐center photoluminescence (PL) from chips fabricated on the mainstream silicon photonics actives platform using a straightforward back‐end‐of‐line (BEOL) recipe. At a 7.0 MeV implant energy, we achieved W‐center photoluminescence with brightness comparable to prior in‐house processes.
